Engagement was defined as the percentage of questions answered among the total number of clips viewed, calculated for each posted story (story engagement, E(s)) and each resident (resident engagement, E(r)). E(s) was tested for an association with (1) weekend vs weekday posts, (2) answering questions correctly vs incorrectly, and (3) supportive responses from faculty vs no feedback.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 16 posts, 120 questions were answered from 428 clips viewed by 35 residents, resulting in an E(s) of 28% (range 15%-59%) across posts and a median E(r) of 19% (IQR 0%-39%) across residents; 71% (n=25) of residents engaged with at least 1 post. E(s) was higher during weekdays vs weekends (30% vs 21%; P=.007) and correlated to answering correctly vs incorrectly (r=0.6; P<.001). A supportive comment resulted in a lower percentage of answering the next post, compared to no feedback (30% vs 71%; P=.02).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Social media engagement was higher when questions were answered correctly but, surprisingly, lower when posts were made on weekends and immediately after receiving a supportive comment.

articles.title: Cardiovascular disease mortality in a Central-West Brazilian capital: A spatial, temporal, and ecological analysis.

abstract.text: In Brazil, regional disparities in cardiovascular disease (CVD) mortality persist, with no population-based study having examined CVD mortality at the municipal level in the Central-West region. This study analysed the epidemiological profile, temporal trends, spatial distribution, and socioeconomic correlates of CVD mortality in Campo Grande, Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil (2013-2022). A population-based ecological study used data from the Brazilian Mortality Information System. Five CVD groups were analysed: ischaemic heart disease (IHD), heart failure (HF), arrhythmias (ARR), cardiomyopathies (CMP), and inflammatory heart diseases (INF). Temporal trends were assessed using Poisson, Prais-Winsten, and Joinpoint regression. Spatial distribution was examined through Kernel Density Estimation and Local Indicators of Spatial Association (LISA). Socioeconomic correlates were assessed using Spearman's correlation with neighbourhood-level indicators. Of 59,392 registered deaths, 8,148 (13.7%) were CVD-related. IHD was the dominant cause (79.5%), with males accounting for 59.3% of deaths (IRR 1.59; 95% CI 1.46-1.74) and individuals aged ≥60 years representing 75.2%. Overall crude CVD mortality increased by 26.1% over the study period, with an estimated mean annual increase of 2.5% (APC + 2.5%/year; 95% CI 1.7-3.3; p < 0.001) and significant acceleration after 2019. A striking proportion of IHD deaths occurred outside hospital settings (67.3%), with home deaths alone surpassing hospital deaths (43.9% vs. 32.7%). Spatial analysis identified significant high-high mortality clusters in central-western neighbourhoods and low-low clusters in eastern neighbourhoods (13 and 5 neighbourhoods, respectively; Global Moran's I = 0.555, p < 0.001), with cluster patterns varying by disease group. Socioeconomic correlates showed a consistent pattern across most CVD groups, with higher mortality in more socioeconomically advantaged neighbourhoods, except for inflammatory heart disease, which showed the opposite pattern. This first municipal-level CVD mortality analysis in Central-West Brazil identified significant spatiotemporal heterogeneity and a high burden of out-of-hospital IHD deaths, providing actionable evidence for geographically targeted cardiovascular prevention strategies.

articles.title: Incidence of Prehospital Delay in People with Ischemic Stroke: A Meta-Analysis.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Intravenous thrombolysis for ischemic stroke can significantly improve neurological outcomes. However, prehospital delay is associated with failure to receive timely treatment and poorer patient outcomes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Nine databases were searched from inception to January 30, 2026. Two researchers independently completed the screening, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment. Incidence rates and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled. Heterogeneity among results was assessed using the I2 statistic. Sensitivity analysis was conducted using the leave-one-out method, and Egger's regression test and funnel plots were used to detect publication bias.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 27 studies involving 266,336 participants across 14 countries were included. The overall pooled incidence was 67.7% (95% CI: 59.2%-75.6%). The pooled incidence of prehospital delay was 65.0% (95% CI: 59.8-70.0%) at the 2-h cut-off, 77.2% (95% CI: 70.2-83.5%) at 3 h, 68.6% (95% CI: 56.2-79.9%) at 3.5 h, 73.8% (95% CI: 60.4-85.3%) at 4 h, and 60.6% (95% CI: 42.8-77.1%) at 4.5 h. The 5- and 6-h cut-offs were each reported by only one study, with incidences of 29.7% and 53.1%, respectively. Subgroup analyses revealed significant moderators, including continent, education level, stroke knowledge, stroke symptom recognition, transportation and study quality. The certainty of evidence was low.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Prehospital delay was common among patients with ischemic stroke, with an overall pooled incidence of 67.7%. Regional estimates varied, but the limited evidence outside Asia and substantial heterogeneity make these comparisons exploratory. Targeted stroke education and improved emergency medical services (EMS) are needed, together with geographically diverse studies using standardized delay definitions.

articles.title: Should MRI Replace Ultrasound as the Primary Imaging Modality in Pediatric Females With Suspected Appendicitis?

abstract.text: Limited sequence, rapid acquisition magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is an established modality for diagnosing appendicitis, but its ability to assess gynecologic pathology remains unclear. We hypothesize that MRI alone sufficiently evaluates reproductive organs in patients with lower abdominal pain. Female patients (<18yo) undergoing MRI in the Emergency Department between January 2019 and January 2025 were reviewed. Patients were stratified into two groups: MRI alone vs pelvic ultrasound (US) and MRI. 142 patients were included with 93 receiving MRI only and 49 receiving both MRI and US. The MRI mentioned evaluation of pelvic structures in 80% of cases. Ovarian cysts were commented on in 5 patients, of which 4 also had US which added no additional information. No gynecologic pathology was missed on MRI. In this study, we found no gynecologic pathology on US that was not also noted on MRI. These findings suggest that an MRI first diagnostic pathway may be sufficient to rule out gynecologic pathology (Table 1).

articles.title: Time toxicity in cancer care: a systematic review of definitions and measurement methods.
articles.journal_full: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: Time toxicity has emerged as an important concept in oncology, reflecting the burden of time patients spend receiving care. However there is no consensus on how time toxicity is defined or measured. We conducted a systematic review to characterise the definitions and measurement methods.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Cochrane Library were searched from inception to 10th March 2026. Studies were included if they involved cancer patients and reported a definable measure of time-related burden associated with care. Data were extracted on study characteristics, sample size, data sources, and definitions of time toxicity.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Fifty-six studies were included. Most studies were observational (n = 45, 80.4%) and conducted in high-income countries, predominantly the United States (n = 29, 51.8%). Time toxicity was most commonly defined using direct healthcare time measures (n = 31, 55.4%), representing days involving healthcare encounters such as clinic visits, treatment sessions, hospitalisations, and emergency department visits. Time away from healthcare measures, including days alive and out of hospital or days at home, were used in 20 studies (35.7%). Healthcare process time incorporating non-clinical and logistical aspects of care were used in 5 studies (8.9%). No studies used patient-reported definitions of time toxicity. Most measures were derived from administrative, electronic health record, or clinical trial data, capturing healthcare utilisation but not patients' perceived burden or value of healthcare-related time.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Current definitions of time toxicity in cancer care are heterogeneous and predominantly system-derived, with minimal incorporation of patient-centred perspectives. We propose an empirical framework comprising three objective measurement domains: direct healthcare time, time away from healthcare, and healthcare process time-with patient-reported experience incorporated as an evidence-informed extension.

articles.title: The utilisation of international consensus definitions of the disease polytrauma: a systematic review.
articles.journal_full: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: The disease of polytrauma is associated with significant healthcare burden and poor prognosis. The validated Newcastle and the Berlin consensus definitions of polytrauma have been proposed more than a decade ago for standardising clinical, scientific and advocacy related communications. This systematic review aims to evaluate the uptake of the Newcastle and the Berlin definitions of polytrauma since their introduction.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This systematic review (PROSPERO: CRD420251119950) adhered to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. A literature search of original research studies reported in English on polytrauma patients from 1st January 2015 to 31st of December 2025 was conducted, using Medline, Embase, Scopus, Pubmed, CINAHL and CENTRAL. Specific focus was on the utilisation of the Berlin and the Newcastle definitions, but all explicitly stated definitions of polytrauma were analysed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 2354 studies were identified through initial literature search. 1491 studies were excluded after screening by title and abstract. The full text review of 863 studies was performed and resulted in 88 eligible studies after the exclusion of 732 studies with no explicit definitions of polytrauma and 43 studies on non-human subjects. Ten studies (11.4%) used the Berlin definition of polytrauma, and six studies (6.8%) reported using the Newcastle definition. The consensus definitions were reported the most in 2024, with 2 studies using Newcastle and 3 studies using the Berlin definition of polytrauma.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Despite the establishment and utility in accurately representing the polytrauma population, the Newcastle and the Berlin definitions of polytrauma remain under-utilised in the current literature.

articles.title: Adhesive small bowel obstruction in the virgin abdomen: comparable phenotype, divergent management.
articles.journal_full: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: In small bowel obstruction (SBO), the absence of prior abdominal surgery is commonly interpreted as a marker of higher-risk pathology and is often associated with a lower threshold for early operative intervention. Whether this assumption reflects differences in disease phenotype or decision-making remains uncertain.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This post hoc analysis of a prospective, multicenter cohort study included consecutive adults with CT-confirmed mechanical SBO. Analyses were restricted to patients with adhesion-related SBO to enable comparison between virgin abdomen adhesive SBO (vaASBO) and prior-surgery adhesive SBO (psASBO). Clinical presentation, imaging findings, management strategies, and 60-day outcomes, including patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs), were evaluated. Analyses were associative and unadjusted.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 1,737 patients, 417 (24.0%) had no prior abdominal surgery; adhesions accounted for 30% of cases in this subgroup. The adhesion-restricted cohort included 982 patients, of whom 127 (12.9%) had vaASBO. Clinical and radiological features were similar between groups; however, management differed substantially. Patients with vaASBO had higher rates of direct-to-surgery (+ 15.0% points), lower use of water-soluble contrast (- 19.1% points), and higher rates of nonoperative management (NOM) failure (+ 25.1% points). Among patients undergoing surgery, complication rates were lower in vaASBO (9.2% vs. 23.3%), with similar rates of major complications, mortality, and length of stay. Among patients successfully managed nonoperatively, clinical outcomes and PROMs were comparable.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In an adhesion-restricted cohort, patients with and without prior abdominal surgery had comparable clinical phenotype, yet management diverged. These findings suggest that surgical history is associated with treatment selection beyond measured markers of disease severity. A CT-guided, risk-stratified approach may provide a more consistent and reproducible basis for decision-making and reduce unnecessary surgery without compromising clinical or patient-reported outcomes.

articles.title: What to do with K-wires in displaced upper extremity fractures in children - where to bury or not.
articles.journal_full: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society

abstract.text: Kirschner wires (K-wires) are the standard fixation method for displaced pediatric upper extremity fractures, yet no consensus exists on whether wire ends should be buried subcutaneously or left exposed epicutaneously. While epicutaneous K-wires offer cost-effectiveness and avoid second anesthesia, concerns remain regarding infection risk and psychological distress. To systematically review and compare complication rates between buried and exposed K-wire fixation in pediatric upper extremity fractures, including infection, refracture, skin erosion, and secondary implant displacement. We conducted a systematic review following PRISMA guidelines, searching Cochrane, PubMed, EmBase, and Ovid databases. Inclusion criteria were: modified Coleman Methodology Score (mCMS) > 60, upper extremity fractures treated with K-wire fixation, and age < 16 years. Studies including adult patients and biomechanical studies were excluded. Meta-analysis compared outcomes across 12 studies encompassing 1,977 patients. Buried K-wires demonstrated significantly lower overall infection rates (OR = 1.74; 95% CI: 1.19-2.56; p = 0.004). However, no significant difference was observed in deep surgical siteinfections (OR = 1.56; 95% CI: 0.60-4.0; p = 0.36). Exposed wires showed significantly lower skin irritation rates (OR = 0.09; 95% CI: 0.04-0.21; p < 0.00001). No significant differences were found in secondary implant displacement (OR = 1.26; 95% CI: 0.10-15.75; p = 0.86) or refracture rates (OR = 1.90; 95% CI: 0.91-3.96; p = 0.09). Geographic subgroup analysis revealed significant regional differences: infection rate differences were significant in Asia/Africa (OR = 2.90; 95% CI: 1.61-5.22; p = 0.0004) but not in Europe/USA (OR = 1.16; 95% CI: 0.69-1.95; p = 0.57). Epicutaneous K-wire fixation shows higher overall infection rates than buried wires but does not increase deep surgical site infections requiring operative revision. Considering the avoidance of additional anesthesia, favorable cost-benefit profile, and geographic variation in infection risk, epicutaneous K-wires are recommended when no patient-specific contraindications exist, particularly in temperate climates. Level III (Systematic Review of Level II-III Studies).

articles.title: Exploring risk groups for concomitant injuries in facial fracture patients: a data-driven analysis.
articles.journal_full: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: Patients with facial fractures are a diverse group with varying injury mechanisms and extent of injury. These patients often suffer from concomitant injuries (CIs) of different severity outside the facial region, some of which are life-threatening and may require urgent care. Therefore, early identification of patients at risk for CI is important. This study aimed to investigate exploratory risk groups for concomitant injuries in patients with facial fractures, focusing on the impact of injury energy, sex and age on the prevalence and type of concomitant injury.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this retrospective cohort study, a data-driven analysis was used to perform statistical analysis and identify risk groups for different CIs. The study included 4170 patients with facial fractures evaluated at tertiary trauma centres from January 2013 to October 2020.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: 70.9% of patients with facial fractures were male. Patients' mean age was 45.7 years. Of the injury mechanisms, 36.0% were classified as high-energy trauma. In all, 31.7% of facial fracture patients had some type of CI. Female patients had more CIs than male patients (34.0% vs. 30.8%). The occurrence of CIs increased progressively with age, peaking in the age group 90-94 years, where over 55% of patients experienced CIs. However, considerable variation was observed in CI types across age groups.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Due to the high CI risk in facial fracture patients, in conjunction with assessment and imaging of the facial trauma, we encourage routinely ruling out CIs, with a special focus on high-risk CI groups.

articles.title: Hydroxyapatite/poly-L-lactide mesh tube versus β-tricalcium phosphate granules in locking plate fixation of proximal humeral fractures: a retrospective comparative study.
articles.journal_full: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: Proximal humeral fractures in older adults are often accompanied by metaphyseal bone defects, leading to reduction loss after plate fixation. Fibular allograft struts provide effective augmentation. However, their availability is limited. This study aimed to compare the outcomes of using hydroxyapatite/poly-L-lactide (HA/PLLA) mesh tubes as endosteal struts and β-tricalcium phosphate (β-TCP) granules for augmentation in locking plate osteosynthesis for proximal humeral fractures.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective study included 42 adult patients who underwent locking plate fixation for acute, closed proximal humeral fractures at a single institution between 2013 and 2022. Among them, 20 patients received endosteal strut-HA/PLLA mesh tube (group E), and 22 received β-TCP granules (group G). Demographics, radiographic outcomes (humeral head height and neck-shaft angle), range of motion, complications, and surgical parameters were compared between the two groups.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Group E showed a significantly smaller mean change in humeral head height than group G (1.5 ± 3.1 vs. 4.0 ± 4.0 mm, p = 0.01). No significant difference in the mean change in neck-shaft angle was observed between the two groups (p = 0.31). Furthermore, no significant differences were observed in shoulder range of motion, complication rates, operative time, or blood loss between the two groups.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The use of HA/PLLA mesh tube as an intramedullary strut in locking plate osteosynthesis provided superior maintenance of humeral head height compared with β-TCP granules, without increasing complications. Endosteal strut-HA/PLLA mesh tubes may be a practical and safe alternative to allograft struts for augmentation in settings where allografts are unavailable.

articles.title: Comment on: Evaluation of thoracolumbar spine injury utilizing plain film and physical examination in the pediatric population: A multicenter study.
articles.journal_full: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery

articles.title: Hamstring Strain Grade on MRI and Return to Play in Elite Australian Cricket Players.
articles.journal_full: Clinical journal of sport medicine : official journal of the Canadian Academy of Sport Medicine

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: The aims of this study were to (1) examine the relationship between magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-confirmed hamstring strain grade and time to return to play; (2) examine this relationship specifically in pace bowlers; and (3) describe the incidence, prevalence, and grade of MRI-confirmed hamstring strains in elite Australian cricket players.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: This is a retrospective cohort study.

abstract.label: SETTING
abstract.text: Elite Australian cricket teams over 13.5 seasons were analyzed.

abstract.label: PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: Four hundred seventy-eight male and 365 female contracted Australian cricketers participated in this study.

abstract.label: INDEPENDENT VARIABLE
abstract.text: British Athletics Muscle Injury Classification system grading of hamstring strains, which had received MRI scan, was the independent variable.

abstract.label: MAIN OUTCOME MEASURE
abstract.text: The main outcome was time to return to play (days).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: One hundred forty-one hamstring strain injuries with available MRI imaging scans were recorded during the study period (average 3.2 per 100 players per season: male 4.5, female 1.2). The most commonly injured muscle was biceps femoris (63%, 95% confidence interval: 56%-71%) and the most frequent category of injury was grade 2C (27%, 20%-35%). Across all injury grades, players were unavailable for full participation for a median of 22 (interquartile range: 15-38) days and missed 3 (1-6) matches. The number of days unavailable were higher for injuries that were graded 2 or 3, compared with grade 1 injuries (P = 0.004 and P = 0.007, respectively), and injuries that included the tendon compared with those which did not (P = 0.002). Pace bowlers has a higher number of days unavailable compared with players with other dominant skills for grade B and C injuries combined (P = 0.046).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This study provides evidence that higher grade injuries and those involving the intramuscular tendon are associated with a more prolonged return to play. This finding should be viewed in context of the study limitation that MRI findings may have informed management.

articles.title: Emergency Nurses' Training, Experience, and Confidence With Obstetrical Emergencies: A Cross-Sectional Survey in Arkansas.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: The United States has the highest maternal mortality rate among high-income countries, with rural states being disproportionately affected. In counties without birthing hospitals, emergency departments can serve as the first point of care for obstetrical complications. This study assessed emergency nurses' experience and confidence in managing obstetrical complications in the rural state of Arkansas.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Emergency nurses at Arkansas hospitals were invited to participate in a cross-sectional survey. The web-based survey asked nurses to report their experience in managing 15 obstetrical complications and their receipt of related training. Confidence in managing complications was assessed using a modified evidence-based practice confidence scale. Statistical analyses included descriptive statistics and multilevel ordinal regression modeling.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The sample included 164 emergency nurses employed across 42 Arkansas hospitals. Over two-thirds of all respondents (70.1%) had received training on at least 1 obstetrical emergency in the 2 years before the survey. Nurses most commonly reported training on pregnancy-related hypertension and seizures (36.6%), postpartum hemorrhage (31.1%), and stabilization of the newborn (27.4%). More than half of the nurses reported high interest in training on 13 obstetrical topics. Nurses' confidence in managing pregnancy-related hypertension was associated with receipt of training, previous case experience, and the presence of inpatient obstetrical services at their hospital.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: This study demonstrates a need to better prepare emergency nurses in Arkansas to manage a range of obstetrical complications. Simulation-based education, which combines experiential learning with didactic instruction, may build the experience and confidence needed to manage obstetrical emergencies in areas with limited obstetrical care.

articles.title: Should Intravenous Loop Diuretics Be Administered Early to All Patients With Acute Heart Failure in the Emergency Department? Yes.
Determinants of Physical Therapy Referral for Peripheral Vestibular Disorders.
articles.journal_full: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To identify patient- and provider-level determinants of PT referrals for peripheral vestibular disorders.

abstract.label: STUDY DESIGN
abstract.text: Retrospective cohort study using electronic health record data.

abstract.label: SETTING
abstract.text: A large health system in western Pennsylvania.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We included individuals 18 years of age or older with a new encounter for a peripheral vestibular disorder between 1/1/2017 and 6/30/2022. The primary outcome was PT referral. Exposures included patient age, gender, race, insurance, urbanization, area deprivation index (ADI), Elixhauser comorbidity index, peripheral vestibular diagnosis, provider type, and specialty.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: We included 20,468 individuals (mean [SD] age 59 [13] years and 69.3% female) with an incident peripheral vestibular disorder visit with 21.7% having a referral to PT. In adjusted models, patients more likely to receive a PT referral were 70 years of age or older (OR = 1.23, 95% CI: 1.04-1.45) versus <50 years of age, female (OR = 1.18, 95% CI: 1.07-1.3), have Medicaid (OR = 1.20, 95% CI: 1.04-1.39) versus commercial insurance, benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (OR = 1.88, 95% CI: 1.57-2.26) versus other peripheral vestibular diagnoses, and 3+ comorbidities (OR = 1.22, 95% CI: 1.07-1.38) versus no comorbidities. Neurology was more likely to refer (OR = 6.10, 95% CI: 2.56-14.58), and emergency medicine was less likely to refer to PT (OR = 0.18, 95% CI: 0.08-0.39) compared to otolaryngology.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This study identified patient- and provider-level determinants of PT referrals for use when identifying strategies to equitably improve PT referrals in health systems.

articles.title: The Associations of Various Types of Hurricane-Related Exposures with Psychiatric and Substance Use Disorders in Puerto Rico Following Hurricane Maria.
articles.journal_full: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To examine the associations between various hurricane-related exposures and psychiatric and substance use disorders among Puerto Rican adults following Hurricane Maria and to identify disaster-related exposures that may contribute to psychiatric morbidity in hurricane- and typhoon-prone settings.

abstract.label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
abstract.text: Hurricane-related exposures were grouped into personal, property, utility/resource losses, and unsanitary/hazardous exposures. Logistic regression models were run to examine the associations between the number of hurricane-related exposures and disorders.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Each additional hurricane-related exposure was associated with a 1.1 percentage-point increase in the probability of any mood disorder (P < 0.001), a 1.3 percentage-point increase in the probability of any anxiety disorder (P < 0.001), and a 2.0 percentage-point increase in the probability of any disorder (P < 0.001). Each additional utility/resource loss exposure was associated with a 2.3 percentage-point increase in the probability of any anxiety disorder (P = 0.001). Each additional unsanitary/hazardous exposure was associated with a 1.9 percentage-point increase in the probability of any mood disorder (P = 0.017). Findings varied when individual disorders were examined. No associations were found between exposures and substance use disorders.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Utility/resource losses and unsanitary/hazardous conditions emerged as important correlates of post-disaster psychiatric disorders, suggesting that these often-overlooked exposures should be incorporated into disaster assessments and recovery planning.

articles.title: A Study on Challenges and Support Needs in Flood Evacuation of Elementary School Students and Their Families in Japan: A Qualitative Study.
articles.journal_full: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: As flood disasters increase with climate change, elementary school children require consideration due to their developing self-protection capacities. However, their specific challenges and support needs during flood evacuation remain inadequately investigated. This study identified challenges faced by elementary school children and their families during flood evacuation and elucidated needed support.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A qualitative study was conducted using semi-structured interviews with 8 parents of 9 elementary school children using maximum variation sampling. Following the COREQ guidelines, interviews focused on the flood evacuation process from onset to shelter arrival. Data were analyzed using Braun and Clarke's reflexive thematic analysis with an inductive analytical framework.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Five major themes were identified from 111 codes (percentages indicate the proportion of total codes): Disaster preparedness (22.5%), Evacuation support (16.2%), Material support at evacuation sites (22.5%), Environmental support at evacuation sites (22.5%), and Disaster response (16.2%). The findings revealed multifaceted challenges and required support systems during flood disasters.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Children's and their families' safety during flood disasters may require enhanced community awareness, family evacuation plans, child-friendly shelters, effective information systems, and collaboration among schools, families, and communities. These findings emphasize considering their unique needs in disaster planning and evacuation shelter management. Future research should develop practical intervention programs with diverse samples to enhance resilience.

articles.title: Violence-Related Emergency Medical Services Encounters in the Anatolian Side of Istanbul: A Retrospective Registry-Based Study.
articles.journal_full: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This study aimed to describe the epidemiological, clinical, and operational characteristics of violence-related emergency medical services (EMS) encounters recorded on the Anatolian side of Istanbul from 2019 to 2023, to conduct secondary descriptive comparisons by sex, and to identify factors associated with confirmed prehospital death status.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective observational registry-based analysis of records coded as "Violence & Assault." Clinical, operational, and demographic variables were analyzed. Comparisons by sex and confirmed death status were conducted using nonparametric and categorical-data tests. In a secondary exploratory analysis, Firth-penalized multivariable logistic regression was used to estimate adjusted associations with confirmed prehospital death status.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The sample comprised 29,335 violence-related EMS encounters; most involved young adult males and occurred in urban districts. Most recorded clinical findings were normal or preserved, although a small subgroup showed physiological instability. Several sex-based differences were statistically significant, but their effect sizes were generally small. Confirmed prehospital death was recorded in 132 encounters (0.45%). In the exploratory Firth model, severe respiratory status (aOR 56.02, 95% CI 8.62-364.05), altered consciousness (aOR 10.71, 95% CI 1.67-68.67), and cyanotic skin (aOR 4.24, 95% CI 2.67-6.73) were associated with the highest adjusted odds ratios for confirmed prehospital death.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Violence-related EMS encounters were concentrated among young adult males, and most did not meet the confirmed-death definition. Nevertheless, a clinically important subgroup presented with physiological instability. In the exploratory analysis, confirmed prehospital death was most strongly associated with acute physiological compromise; operational intervals should be interpreted cautiously as potential markers of case complexity and EMS workflow rather than as causal determinants.

articles.title: Footwraps as a Sock Alternative in Disaster Settings: Insights From Trench Foot Prevention.
articles.journal_full: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Trench foot develops after prolonged exposure of the feet to cold, wet conditions (e.g., during floods in cold climates), causing pain, swelling, and impaired gait. It can be prevented by maintaining dry feet and changing socks whenever they become wet. However, sock shortages are common in disaster settings. A practical alternative is cloth footwrapping. This study evaluated footwrap skill acquisition across different age groups and assessed the feasibility of footwraps as sock substitutes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A total of 100 laypersons from four age groups completed 10 footwrapping trials. Subsequently, participants performed walking trials wearing shoes, with one foot wrapped and the other unwrapped. Technique acquisition and sock-substitution outcomes were analyzed statistically. Stability, shoe tightness, and acceptability were summarized as frequencies.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Achieving optimal footwrap tightness was the most challenging aspect of the technique. Participants aged ≥70 years required more trials and time to acquire the technique. Footwraps showed favorable results across most sock-substitution measures, except for friction-related pain reduction. Among the participants, 17 experienced loosening within 30 min, 2 reported shoe tightness, and all indicated a willingness to use footwraps as sock substitutes in shelters.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Footwraps may be practical sock alternatives in resource-limited environments; however, age-related differences in skill acquisition warrant tailored instruction.

articles.title: Conflict-Related WASH System Failure and Public Health Preparedness in the Middle East: A Policy-Oriented Narrative Review.
articles.journal_full: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness

abstract.text: Conflicts in the Middle East have intensified public health emergencies through progressive failure of water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) systems. This policy-oriented narrative review synthesizes peer-reviewed and humanitarian evidence published between January 2020 and March 2026 on WASH system failure and related public health consequences in Gaza and the occupied Palestinian territory, Yemen, Syria, Lebanon, and Iraq. Across these settings, four recurring mechanisms emerged: physical damage; loss of electricity, fuel, chemicals, and spare parts; restrictions on access and workforce safety; and governance, financing, and coordination failures. These mechanisms impaired water treatment and distribution, wastewater and waste management, and hygiene in health care facilities. The evidence documented plausible pathways connecting these failures to diarrheal illness, cholera, hepatitis A, environmental exposure, and weakened infection prevention and control, although disrupted surveillance limited causal attribution. The settings also showed distinct patterns, ranging from acute infrastructure damage in Gaza to protracted institutional attrition in Yemen and Syria, conflict spillover and economic stress in Lebanon, and episodic vulnerability in Iraq. The review advances a cross-setting failure-to-harm pathway and a phased preparedness framework. Immediate priorities are protecting WASH workers and assets, sustaining energy and critical inputs, and linking WASH indicators with health surveillance; medium-term recovery requires service restoration, workforce capacity, and coordinated financing; and long-term resilience requires decentralized, redundant, conflict-resilient systems.

articles.title: Hyperammonaemia in Neonatal Transport: A Retrospective Statewide Review of Neonates Retrieved With Elevated Ammonia.
articles.journal_full: Journal of paediatrics and child health

abstract.label: AIMS
abstract.text: To characterise the aetiology, retrieval characteristics and outcomes of neonatal hyperammonaemia in a statewide neonatal retrieval service.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Retrospective chart review of all neonates (aged ≤ 8 weeks) retrieved by the statewide Paediatric Infant Perinatal Emergency Retrieval (PIPER) service to the Royal Children's Hospital (RCH), Melbourne, Australia, between April 2016 and February 2025, with a pre-transport plasma ammonia > 100 μmol/L.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Twenty-one neonates met inclusion criteria. Median gestation was 38 weeks (IQR: 38-39) and median age at retrieval referral was 59 h (IQR: 48-84). A confirmed inborn error of metabolism (IEM) was identified in 16 of 21 neonates (76%), with urea cycle disorders accounting for 12 of the 16 confirmed IEMs (75%). Twelve patients (57%) required continuous veno-venous haemofiltration (CVVHF). Compared with those managed without haemofiltration, the CVVHF group had higher peak ammonia (median 854 vs. 378 μmol/L) and a higher rate of confirmed IEM (92% vs. 56%). Twelve retrievals (57%) were classified as time-critical, and metabolic medication was administered during transport in nine cases (43%). Median time from decision to retrieve to team dispatch was 20 min (IQR: 13-26) and to specialist hospital arrival 152 min (IQR: 97-229). Seventeen neonates (81%) survived to hospital discharge.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Neonatal hyperammonaemia requiring retrieval is predominantly caused by an IEM and frequently requires CVVHF, with low occurrence of spurious elevation. These findings support early retrieval to a quaternary centre with haemofiltration capability and provide benchmarking data for retrieval services managing this rare, high-acuity condition.

articles.title: "I Just Knew That I Needed Help": Primarily Latine Adolescents and Young Adults Speak About Medication Treatment for Opioid Use Disorder in the Fentanyl Era.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Medications for opioid use disorder (MOUD) are evidence-based, lifesaving treatments for adolescents and young adults (AYAs) with opioid use disorder (OUD). However, AYAs access MOUD at alarmingly low rates. Therefore, this study investigated facilitators, barriers, and health services preferences for accessing MOUD among AYAs desiring treatment for OUD within a safety-net health system.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted 11 semi-structured interviews with AYAs aged 16 to 21 who initiated MOUD in a county safety-net health system. Patients started MOUD (primarily buprenorphine) in inpatient, outpatient, and/or emergency department settings. We employed combined inductive and deductive coding and thematic analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Ten of 11 (91%) AYAs identified as Latine, and 9 (82%) were publicly insured. We identified 4 themes: (1) AYAs weighed the consequences of ongoing non-prescribed opioid use when deciding to engage in treatment; (2) perceived therapeutic and adverse effects of MOUD influenced AYAs' desire to start and continue MOUD; (3) Relationships with peers, caregivers, parole officers, and healthcare providers enabled AYAs to start and continue OUD treatment; (4) Inpatient MOUD initiation experiences were largely positive, though a few had negative experiences.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This predominantly publicly insured, Latine sample of AYAs with OUD identified relationships, perceived risks of opioids, and perceived effectiveness of MOUD as key facilitators to engage in MOUD. Also, AYAs largely appreciated starting MOUD inpatient, though many identified barriers to continuing MOUD long-term. These perspectives provide essential input into future research, clinical, and public health interventions.

articles.title: Plate-Based Operative Management of Medial Malleolar Stress Fractures in High-Level Basketball Players: A Short Report.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Medial malleolar stress fractures (MMSFs) are uncommon but potentially high-risk injuries in athletes. In basketball players, repetitive jumping, landing, and cutting may expose the characteristic vertical fracture pattern to substantial shear, yet sport-specific operative data remain limited. This study reports the outcomes of plate-based fixation for MMSFs in high-level basketball players.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective case series was performed of 10 high-level basketball players treated surgically for MMSF between 2007 and 2025. All patients underwent radiography, magnetic resonance imaging, and computed tomography (CT). Operative treatment consisted of shear resisting plate-based fixation (one-third tubular anti-glide or hook plate) with fracture-perpendicular screws, selective bone grafting, biologic augmentation, and treatment of associated anterior impingement when indicated. Primary outcomes were radiographic union, return to play, and need for additional surgery.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: All patients were male, with a median age of 20.5 years (range, 18-26). Median height was 205.5 cm (IQR, 198-213), and the median weight was 103.5 kg (IQR, 93-113). Eight players were professional and 2 were collegiate athletes later drafted professionally. CT demonstrated a vertically oriented fracture arising from the anteromedial tibial plafond in all cases. Union was achieved in all players. Nine returned to full team activities by 12 weeks and to competitive play at a median of 4 months (range, 3-4 months). One player sustained a traumatic refracture 8 months after index fixation, required 2 revision procedures, ultimately healed after supplemental anterior plating, and returned to play at 6 months.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Plate-based fixation was associated with reliable union and return to play, although revision surgery was required in 1 of 10 players. Given the consistent vertical fracture morphology and substantial sport-specific loading demands, shear resisting plating may be considered in this population.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: Level IV, case series.

articles.title: Impact of Inaccurate Pretriage Labeling at Advanced Medical Post Entry on Time-Critical Care Processes: A Pilot Simulation Study at the World Economic Forum.
articles.journal_full: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness

abstract.label: BACKGROUND AND IMPORTANCE
abstract.text: In mass-casualty incidents, inaccurate pretriage labeling at Advanced Medical Post (AMP) arrival, whether due to undertriage or clinical deterioration before arrival, may affect downstream workflow processes and delay recognition of critically injured patients. Although triage accuracy has been widely studied, the operational impact of inaccurate pretriage labelling at AMP entry on time-critical care processes within AMP systems remains poorly understood.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To evaluate the impact of inaccurate pretriage labeling at AMP entry on downstream time-critical care processes in simulated red-category patients.

abstract.label: DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: Prospective, pilot simulation-based study conducted during 2 full-scale AMP exercises. The AMP reflected the real-world operational structure, personnel, and logistics of an AMP deployed during the World Economic Forum (WEF) 2026. Each simulation included 18 standardized patients; 10 met predefined red-triage criteria and constituted the analytic cohort. The primary objective was to compare time to predefined first critical action between correctly labeled and mislabeled patients.

abstract.label: EXPOSURE
abstract.text: Mislabeled at AMP entry, defined as red patients entering the AMP undertriaged with a lower-acuity pretriage label (yellow instead of red).

abstract.label: OUTCOMES MEASURE AND ANALYSIS
abstract.text: The primary outcome was time from AMP entry to first predefined critical action. Secondary outcomes included reaching predefined case-specific deterioration or death thresholds prior to intervention and time to correction of triage category. Outcomes were analyzed descriptively using within-patient paired comparisons across simulation runs.

abstract.label: MAIN RESULTS
abstract.text: Across 2 simulation runs, 6 paired observations were analyzed. In 4 of 5 comparisons in which a predefined critical action was performed, mislabeling was associated with longer time to predefined critical action, with delays ranging from 5 to 24 minutes. In 2 cases, these delays resulted in crossing of case-specific deterioration thresholds. In 1 additional mislabeled patient, the predefined critical action was not performed before the deterioration threshold was reached, and the patient subsequently progressed to the scripted death threshold. No correctly labelled red patient reached deterioration or death. Early correction of triage status mitigated delays, whereas delayed correction was associated with adverse progression.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In this pilot full-scale simulation study, inaccurate pretriage labeling at AMP entry was associated with delays in time-critical interventions. These findings highlight the importance of early and continuous structured reassessment and timely correction of triage categorization within AMP workflows. The results are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in further simulation or real-world studies.

articles.title: Mpox Vaccine Acceptance Among Health Care Workers in Central Asia: The Role of COVID-19 Experience.
articles.journal_full: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The COVID-19 pandemic may have shaped health care workers' (HCWs') perceptions of emerging infectious threats and willingness to adopt new vaccines. This study examined whether COVID-19-related experiences and psychological factors were associated with Mpox vaccine acceptance among HCWs in Central Asia.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this cross-sectional study, 3,054 HCWs from Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and Uzbekistan completed an online survey between July and November 2022. Mpox vaccine acceptance was assessed using a single 5-point Likert-scale item and analyzed as a continuous outcome. Measures included COVID-19-related experiences, fear of COVID-19 and Mpox, DASS-21, and occupational burnout. Analyses included comparative tests, multivariable linear regression, and exploratory mediation models.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Overall, 1,868 HCWs (61.2%) reported some willingness to receive Mpox vaccination, whereas 1,186 (38.8%) reported none. In bivariate analyses, acceptance varied by country and was higher among HCWs with COVID-19 frontline experience or living with high-risk individuals. In multivariable regression, fear of Mpox was the strongest correlate of acceptance, while burnout was inversely associated. Mediation analyses indicated indirect associations through fear- and distress-related pathways.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Mpox vaccine acceptance among Central Asian HCWs was associated with pandemic experience and psychological responses to infectious disease risk. Strategies should combine risk communication with burnout reduction and HCW well-being support.

articles.title: The SHARE-HRS ScRAPS Model of Scarce Health Resource Allocation in Humanitarian Response Settings: Thematic Analysis of Lived Experiences.
articles.journal_full: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: The aim of this research is to explore and report on factors that define and impact resource availability and the decision-making space regarding scarce health resources in humanitarian response settings.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This research was conducted with an exploratory qualitative design. Clinicians and managers with relevant experience were identified and purposively recruited to include broad perspectives. Semi-structured interviews were conducted remotely to produce transcripts of participant narrative which were analyzed using an inductive thematic analysis approach to allow themes to arise from the data.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Seventeen interviews were conducted, contributing 887 minutes of data. Five themes framing decision-making were identified: scope; relationships; adaptation; power; and security. Each theme influences resource availability and the experience of health resource allocation decisions in humanitarian contexts. Collectively, the themes informed the development of the Scarce Health Resource Allocation in Humanitarian Response Settings (SHARE-HRS) ScRAPS Model.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The findings of this research articulate several pertinent factors that shape resource allocation decision-making in humanitarian health responses. In consolidating these factors, the resulting ScRAPS Model provides a conceptualization and analytical framework for considering humanitarian health responses. Finally, this research illuminates a potential path for future research and communicating learned lessons through a proposed common language.

articles.title: A U.S. Emergency Manager's View of the Water Systems Crisis in Gaza.
articles.journal_full: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness

abstract.text: Before October 2023, Gaza's water sector already faced severe and persistent challenges, including aquifer contamination, damaged infrastructure, and limited system reliability. The ongoing armed conflict has intensified these conditions, causing unprecedented destruction and the near-total breakdown of water and wastewater services. The conflict itself continues to obstruct remediation, mitigation, and broader efforts to address the longstanding public health crisis.Many residents now depend on brackish well water, limited desalination output, or imported bottled water because local systems cannot provide consistently reliable and safe drinking water. Access to clean water remains a critical humanitarian concern, with repeated disruptions caused by damaged pipelines, fuel and parts shortages for water pumps, and restrictions on the import of repair materials. From an emergency management perspective, this constitutes a chronic disaster with urgent and unresolved life-safety consequences.Gaza's wastewater infrastructure has also sustained extensive damage, leaving large portions of the system inoperable. Damage to treatment plants and sewage pipelines has led to repeated sewage overflows and the discharge of untreated wastewater into the environment, including discharge of untreated sewage into the Mediterranean and the flow of sewage near displacement sites. These failures heighten public health risks by increasing exposure to contaminated drinking water, waterborne disease, and broader environmental pollution/contamination, including direct human exposure to sewage-contaminated coastal water.This paper posits that protecting civilians' health and restoring essential water and wastewater services remain central to any response, and suggests applying the relatively new U.S.-based Community Lifelines concept for emergency management to help prioritize critical infrastructure restoration. It will examine the crisis in Gaza through a U.S. emergency management lens-a view not previously taken by disaster researchers-with particular attention to the humanitarian and ethical imperative to prioritize life safety before, during, and after any type of disaster, via the WASH-Health nexus.

articles.title: Impact of motorcycle ambulances on prehospital response time: a systematic review.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Urban traffic congestion and limited ambulance fleets are associated with prolonged Emergency Medical Services (EMS) response times and worse outcomes in time-critical conditions. To reduce response times, many EMS agencies in large cities have introduced motorcycle ambulance services.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We systematically reviewed English-language literature from January 2008 to November 2025 in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and Google Scholar, following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias. Inclusion criteria were original peer-reviewed studies evaluating motorcycle-based EMS units with quantitative prehospital time outcomes. Given substantial heterogeneity in designs and settings, we performed a qualitative synthesis without meta-analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 713 records identified, 7 studies met inclusion criteria. Included studies reported that motorcycle ambulances generally achieved shorter response times than standard ambulances in congested urban settings. Where numerical estimates were extractable, reported differences ranged from approximately 30 seconds to 2-3 minutes faster response with motorcycle units; one study reported an approximately 23.5% reduction in unnecessary car-ambulance dispatches. However, confidence intervals and adjusted statistical indicators were inconsistently reported. Motorcycle deployment was also associated with fewer unnecessary ambulance dispatches, particularly for low-acuity calls.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Motorcycle ambulances may improve prehospital EMS response times, particularly in congested urban areas and settings with limited road infrastructure. Available studies reported favorable point estimates, but the evidence base is small, heterogeneous, and predominantly observational, with limited data on patient outcomes, safety, and cost-effectiveness. No pooled effect estimate can be justified. Further high-quality studies are needed to clarify the benefits, risks, and optimal role of motorcycle-based EMS within broader emergency care systems.

articles.title: Access to supervised consumption services in the emergency department: patient characteristics and outcomes.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Supervised consumption services have rarely been integrated into hospital environments. This study aimed to describe the characteristics of the first 50 emergency department (ED) patients who accessed a hospital-based supervised consumption service. A secondary goal was to evaluate any adverse events.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This study was carried out in a large urban acute care emergency department. Using a standardized data abstraction template, characteristics of the patient, emergency department visit, and supervised consumption visit were independently extracted by two reviewers from the patient's chart and electronic health record. Descriptive statistics are shown.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The first 50 emergency department patients to access the hospital-based supervised consumption service made a total of 66 visits between October 3, 2019, and September 10, 2020. Most were male (31, 62%) and were sleeping in shelters or outside (30, 60%); 15 (30%) were prescribed opioid agonist treatment in the community. Hospital admission was necessary for 19 patients (38%). Adverse events were infrequent.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Emergency department patients are open to using supervised consumption services. Further research is needed to explore how access to supervised substance use in the emergency department influences patient and staff safety.

articles.title: Association between perioperative antidepressant use and postoperative outcomes after cutaneous melanoma resection.

abstract.text: Cutaneous melanoma is the fifth most common cancer in the USA and the most fatal form of skin cancer. Antidepressants (ADPs) are among the most commonly prescribed medications in this population and may influence postoperative recovery through effects on platelet aggregation, immune signaling, and pain modulation. This study aimed to determine whether perioperative ADP use is associated with increased postoperative complications and healthcare utilization following melanoma resection. Using the TriNetX federated database, we conducted a propensity-matched retrospective cohort study comparing 90-day postoperative outcomes between adult melanoma patients with and without perioperative ADP use following surgical resection. Among 19 470 propensity-matched patients (9735 per group), ADP use was associated with significantly higher rates of opioid prescriptions (32.8% vs 21.2%), surgical site infection (2.1% vs 1.1%), sepsis (1.2% vs 0.4%), inpatient hospitalization (10.7% vs 5.2%), emergency department visits (6.9% vs 4.5%), and hemorrhage (0.3% vs 0.1%; all P < 0.01). Patients in the control cohort were more likely to undergo lymph node biopsy than ADP users (1.3% vs 0.9%; P = 0.006). Wound disruption did not differ significantly between groups. Perioperative ADP use was associated with increased postoperative morbidity and healthcare utilization. Because tumor characteristics and procedural complexity could not be assessed in this dataset, these findings are best interpreted as identifying ADP use as a marker of a higher-risk perioperative phenotype rather than evidence of a direct causal effect. These results support proactive monitoring, infection surveillance, and judicious opioid prescribing in this population.

articles.title: In-hospital antimicrobial use and multidrug-resistant infections among COVID-19 patients in Northern Malaysia (COVAM): a multicentre study.
articles.journal_full: Journal of pharmaceutical policy and practice

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: During the COVID-19 pandemic, empirical antimicrobials were frequently prescribed despite low documented rates of bacterial and fungal co-infections. While early pandemic data exist, evidence evaluating antimicrobial consumption and multidrug-resistant organism (MDRO) dynamics during subsequent pandemic surges remains limited. This study evaluated antimicrobial receipt, associated factors, and the prevalence of MDROs among hospitalised COVID-19 patients in Northern Malaysia.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This multicentre retrospective observational cohort study included adults (≥18 years) with confirmed COVID-19 admitted to ten government hospitals in Northern Malaysia between February 2020 and December 2021. Among 19,116 admissions, 480 cases were sampled, yielding 476 eligible patients. Study outcomes included antimicrobial receipt and MDRO prevalence. Monthly antimicrobial days of therapy (DOT) per 1,000 patient-days were compared with state-level COVID-19 hospital admissions. Predictors were analysed using a Poisson Generalized Linear Mixed Model.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Antibiotics were prescribed to 167 patients (35.1%), accounting for 381 prescriptions, predominantly β-lactam/β-lactamase inhibitors (54.1%). Most were empirical (92.9%), largely among non-ICU patients (72.2%) with pneumonia (82.9%). Antifungals were used in 13 patients (2.7%; 15 prescriptions), mainly empirical echinocandins (60.0%), and predominantly in ICU settings (66.7%). MDROs were detected in 8.4% (10/119) of patients with cultured specimens, representing patient-level MDRO prevalence. A significant positive correlation was observed between DOT and admissions (r = 0.701, p < 0.001, 95% CI [0.37-0.87]). Severe/critical COVID-19 stage, diabetes mellitus, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and chronic kidney disease were consistently associated with antimicrobial prescription. Longer hospital stays, elevated neutrophil and C-reactive protein levels, smoking, and pre-hospital steroid/immunosuppressant use were additional predictors.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Antimicrobial use was predominantly empirical and influenced by disease severity and admission surges. Although MDRO detection remained low, severity-driven prescribing highlights the risk of unnecessary antimicrobial exposure during pandemic waves. These findings inform outbreak-responsive antimicrobial stewardship strategies and support antimicrobial utilisation surveillance to guide resource planning during future public health emergencies.

articles.title: Nurse-led prehospital obstetric care through the lens of the Three Delays Model: an experience report.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: to report the care provided by nurses in the transportation module of the Cegonha Carioca Program, establishing connections with the Three Delays Model.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: experience report describing the care delivered by nurses to pregnant and postpartum women from 2012 to 2024, based on lived experience, public data, and the scientific literature.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: public awareness of the ambulance service, along with the quality and humanization of care, aligns with reducing the delay in seeking care; Free access to the service, the strategic location of ambulances, and the presence of a designated referral maternity hospital facilitate the identification of and access to health services; Efficient communication, prioritization of care, and alert systems support timely and appropriate care.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: care provided in the ambulance is grounded in a humanized model and includes actions aimed at preventing delays. This modality of care is believed to represent a model of prehospital obstetric assistance capable of reducing maternal mortality.

articles.title: Nephrology services during Hajj: A mature model of mass-gathering kidney care.
articles.journal_full: Saudi journal of kidney diseases and transplantation : an official publication of the Saudi Center for Organ Transplantation, Saudi Arabia

articles.title: LOOP DIURETICS SHOULD NOT BE ADMINISTERED EARLY TO ALL PATIENTS WITH ACUTE HEART FAILURE IN THE EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT.
Improving paediatric asthma outcomes in rural settings: clinical effectiveness of a multicomponent asthma care model.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Asthma is a leading cause of childhood hospitalisation and emergency department (ED) presentations in Australia. Barriers persist in accessing paediatric asthma care, particularly in rural areas. We implemented and evaluated a multicomponent model to reduce preventable hospital presentations across rural New South Wales.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted pre-post evaluation of children aged 5-12 years with asthma exacerbations across 13 hospitals in four rural NSW health districts. Children received: 1) a standardised discharge pack, 2) general practitioners (GP) and school linkage, 3) text reminders, and 4) nurse-led virtual home visits for uncontrolled asthma. Primary outcome was healthcare utilisation (ED presentations, admissions and GP visits) from electronic records, comparing matched pre-post periods at 1, 3, 6 and 12 months. Secondary outcomes included asthma control and quality of life at 6 and 12 months. Analyses used generalised estimating equations and mixed-effects models to calculate adjusted rate ratios (aRRs) and mean differences.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: 188 children participated (62% male, mean age 7.6 years). ED presentations decreased 93% at 1 month (aRR 0.07, 95% confidence interval 0.04-0.12), 85% at 3 months (aRR 0.15, 0.10-0.22), 78% at 6 months (aRR 0.22, 0.16-0.30) and 69% at 12 months (aRR 0.31, 0.25-0.40). Hospital admissions decreased 97%, 95%, 90% and 81%. Uncontrolled asthma decreased from 73% to 37% (6 months) and 30% (12 months). Asthma control and quality of life improved significantly at both timepoints.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This multisite study achieved sustained reductions in preventable hospitalisations and meaningful improvements in asthma control and quality of life. This model offers a replicable approach for underserved populations.

articles.title: Enhancing Patient Throughput Through Front-end Redesign and Alternate Care Space Implementation in a Pediatric Emergency Department: A Quality Improvement Initiative.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Emergency department (ED) crowding remains a persistent national challenge, contributing to delays in care, increased length of stay (LOS), and higher rates of patients leaving without being seen (LWBS). Front-end strategies improve throughput and reduce LWBS by enabling earlier assessment and disposition. Building on prior efforts, this quality improvement initiative aimed to enhance patient flow for low-acuity pediatric patients by leveraging alternative care spaces to reduce roomed-to-disposition time, LOS, and LWBS while preserving capacity for higher acuity care.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This initiative occurred in a high-volume pediatric ED using a front-end, physician-driven "Intake" model. To improve efficiency and throughput, the team introduced an alternate care space. Additional interventions included role clarification, workflow standardization, and targeted education for physicians and staff to reduce roomed-to-disposition time for Intake patients by 10% within 4 months.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Roomed-to-disposition time for all Intake patients decreased by 15% (from 88 to 75 min), whereas a specific group of low-intervention patients experienced a 49% reduction. LOS for all Intake patients decreased by 30%, and by 48% for low-intervention patients (from 286 to 148 min). Additional improvements included a 49% reduction in LWBS and a 37% decrease in arrival-to-provider time.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Our quality improvement initiative demonstrated that a thoughtful reorganization of existing ED Intake processes, without additional staffing or physical expansion, can meaningfully improve patient throughput, provider efficiency, and overall ED performance.

articles.title: Clinical outcomes for emergency department patients diagnosed with pubic rami fractures.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: This study aimed to describe the demographics and outcomes of older adults diagnosed with a pubic rami fracture in an Irish emergency department (ED).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective single centre chart review was conducted on all patients diagnosed with pubic rami fracture between 2022 and 2024.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: 131 patients with a pubic rami fracture were identified. 89 (67.9%) were aged 65 and older. 67 (75%) were female. 101 (77.1%) patients required admission. For admitted patients, the mean hospital length of stay (days) was also longer in the older cohort compared to the younger cohort (26.2 versus 8.9, p<0.05).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Pubic rami fracture have a preponderance in older female patients and are associated with high admission rates and hospital length of stays.

articles.title: Early plasma administration in traumatic brain injuries: A systematic review.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Early plasma may improve trauma resuscitation by addressing shock and coagulopathy, but its role in traumatic brain injury (TBI) remains uncertain. This systematic review evaluated early plasma in TBI.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This review followed Cochrane methodology and was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261357882). MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane databases, and Web of Science were searched on February 3, 2026 and rerun August 11, 2026. Comparative studies of prehospital or early in-hospital plasma in TBI were eligible. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB-2 and ROBINS-I, certainty using GRADE, and findings were synthesized narratively.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Fifteen studies including 183,253 patients were included. Studies varied in design, population, plasma product, timing, dose, comparator, and outcomes. A secondary analysis of a cluster-randomized trial found lower 24-h and 30-day mortality with prehospital plasma among patients at risk of hemorrhagic shock subsequently found to have CT-confirmed TBI; the association was observed among direct scene transports but not interfacility transfers, suggesting timing relative to injury may be important. Two small early in-hospital trials showed no mortality benefit; one reported similar mortality with plasma and saline, while the other reported higher mortality and more delayed or new intracranial hematomas with plasma. Observational findings were inconsistent and limited by confounding by indication, with variation by plasma timing, comparator, and TBI severity. Certainty of evidence was very low.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Evidence is insufficient to determine whether early plasma benefits or harms patients with TBI. Future randomized trials should standardize indications, time-to-plasma, plasma protocols, and outcomes and clarify clinically relevant plasma timing windows.

articles.title: Old disease, new twist.

abstract.text: An 81-year-old man with a history of high-grade urothelial carcinoma of the bladder and ureter on treatment with atezolizumab and tiragolumab presented to the emergency department with 5 months of malaise, generalized weakness, and fatigue and 2 weeks of subjective fevers. One month prior to presentation, he received an empiric 9-day course of levofloxacin for possible epididymitis based on scrotal pain and an ultrasound showing mild bilateral epididymal prominence. Blood and urine cultures were negative. His constitutional symptoms persisted, and he developed a subjective fever 2 weeks prior to presentation. He was admitted for further evaluation.

articles.title: Caregivers' reported views on firearm counseling.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Firearm related injuries are the leading cause of death in children older than one year of age. Safety counseling and prevention are cornerstones of injury prevention. This survey study sought to assess caregivers' recollection of firearm safety counseling and who provided that counseling in the past two years. It further sought to determine whom they entrusted to provide this information, and their preferred modalities for future counseling. Secondary objectives included assessing the relationship between parental perspectives on who provided this counseling and how this counseling was provided based on presence of a firearm in the home.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A prospective cross-sectional survey was implemented at a single institution's pediatric emergency department. Parents of children birth-18 years of age were recruited between November 2020 through May 2022, in a private ED treatment room and the survey was administered using a handheld tablet. Excluded were parents of critically ill/injured children (ESI level 1) or those presenting with a primary psychiatric complaint such as suicidal ideation. Chi-square analyses were performed to assess differences in recollection and perception of firearm counseling measures between caregivers who owned a firearm and those who did not.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 820 of 1,181 of eligible caregivers were recruited (response rate of eligible caregivers: 69.4%). 24.1% of respondents recall receiving counseling on firearm safety within the last two years. 56.1% responded affirmatively that pediatricians ought to counsel parents/guardians on firearm safety. 17.4% reported having a firearm in their home, and these respondents were more likely to have received recent safety counseling. Police departments and pediatricians were the most trusted sources for information; with 58.3% and 55.5% of caregivers identifying them as a highly reputable source of such counseling respectively.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Parents are receptive to firearm related counseling by pediatricians and may benefit from learning about the AAP guidelines for firearm and ammunition storage.

articles.title: Automated Derivation of Cerebral Performance Category at Hospital Discharge After Cardiac Arrest Using Natural Language Processing and Machine Learning.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Clinical notes in the electronic health record (EHR) contain rich information that may be leveraged for automated prognostication using natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning. We evaluated the performance and potential biases of an NLP-based machine learning model for deriving cerebral performance category (CPC) for comatose patients following cardiac arrest using EHR clinical notes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adult patients who were comatose after in-hospital or out-of-hospital cardiac arrest across three academic hospitals in the USA. Neurological outcomes were assessed at hospital discharge, with CPC scores of 1-3 indicating good outcomes and 4-5 indicating poor outcomes. An NLP-based logistic regression model was trained on 249 patients using all clinical notes throughout hospitalization. Model performance was evaluated on a holdout set of 108 patients. Performance was also evaluated on the holdout set using only notes documented within the first 24 h of hospitalization.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Using all clinical notes, the model achieved an overall accuracy of 81%, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.90 and an area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) of 0.89. When restricted to notes documented within the first 24 h of hospitalization, model accuracy decreased to 74%, with AUROC of 0.83 and AUPRC of 0.83. The model demonstrated higher precision in predicting poor neurological outcomes, particularly among patients who underwent withdrawal of life-sustaining therapy.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: An NLP-based machine learning model demonstrated high accuracy in deriving CPC for comatose patients after cardiac arrest using EHR clinical notes. Clinical documentation within 24 h after cardiac arrest contained substantial prognostic signals about neurological outcomes, reflecting a combination of patient biology, clinician assessment, and potentially early prognostic framing. Future research should incorporate multimodal data and employ interpretable advanced language models to increase accuracy toward fully automatable CPC derivation.

articles.title: Prevalence of Lyme disease in patients with peripheral facial palsy in the province of Quebec: a prospective multicenter Canadian study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Lyme disease is a recognized cause of peripheral facial palsy, but its estimated prevalence in affected patients varies widely, ranging from 2 to 65%. There are no clear guidelines to assist clinicians in the empiric management of undifferentiated peripheral facial palsy in regions where Lyme disease is prevalent. This prospective multicenter study aimed to determine the prevalence of Lyme disease-associated facial palsy in patients presenting with peripheral facial palsy in four emergency departments in the most endemic regions of Quebec, Canada (Estrie and Montérégie).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Emergency physicians at four Quebec hospitals completed a brief online questionnaire for each patient presenting with peripheral facial palsy from February 2022 to September 2023; they were also encouraged to order Lyme disease testing. A subsequent search was conducted in the electronic medical records of each participating hospital to retrieve Borrelia burgdorferi serology results (ELISA and/or Western blot).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among the 83 patients who consulted for peripheral facial palsy, Lyme disease serology testing was performed in 68 cases. Of these, only two had a positive ELISA screening test. None of these patients had a confirmed diagnosis based on confirmatory Western blot testing.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The findings of this study indicate a low prevalence of Lyme disease among patients presenting with peripheral facial palsy in Quebec. While the authors recommend testing for Lyme disease as per local guidelines in patients presenting with peripheral facial palsy in endemic regions, empiric treatment should not be routinely initiated in the absence of other clinical signs or symptoms suggestive of the disease given the absence of confirmed cases in this cohort.

articles.title: Predictive ability of two frailty screening tools for older patients in an emergency department: a comparative study.

abstract.text: Frailty identification is crucial for guiding individualized treatment in emergency geriatric care. The aims were to prospectively evaluate frailty status in all patients aged 65 and older presenting with acute illness in the emergency department (ED), and to compare the predictive performance of bedside-assessed Brief Multidimensional Prognostic Index (B-MPI), with healthcare professional-assessed Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS) for unplanned readmissions and 30- and 90-day mortality. This prospective observational cohort study evaluated frailty status in 402 patients aged 65 years or older admitted to the ED at Aarhus University Hospital, Denmark, between April 2023 and January 2025 and included through convenience sampling. Frailty was assessed using two validated tools: the CFS, administered by physicians or geriatric healthcare staff, and the B-MPI, administered bedside incorporating patient interviews or caregiver input, and electronic medical record data. Data showed that 40% of the older patients were classified as frail by the CFS, while 50% were moderately or severely frail according to the B-MPI. Both tools predicted 30-day and 90-day mortality with no difference in accuracy for predicting mortality. Neither tool effectively predicted unplanned hospital readmissions. Mortality rates in the cohort were 5.7% at 30 days and 12.9% at 90 days post-admission.
