articles.title: Development and Temporal Validation of a Logistic Regression-Based Risk Score for Identifying Life-Threatening Chest Pain at Emergency Department Triage: A Retrospective Cohort Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Chest pain is a frequent emergency department (ED) presentation with highly time-dependent outcomes. Widely used risk tools such as HEART and GRACE incorporate laboratory results that are unavailable at first nurse contact, limiting their value for immediate triage. In mainland China, acuity assignment follows the Chinese Emergency Triage Scale (CETS), yet nurse triage accuracy remains variable, particularly among less experienced staff.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To develop and temporally validate a simplified, non-laboratory clinical risk score that identifies life-threatening conditions (LTCs)-defined as final physician-assigned CETS Level I or II-among adults presenting to the ED with chest pain, and to map score thresholds onto the four-level CETS framework for nurse-facing decision support.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This was a single-centre retrospective observational cohort study, reported in accordance with TRIPOD+AI, at an ED of a large tertiary academic hospital in Hefei, Anhui Province, China. The cohort was split by calendar time into an internal development cohort (n = 2,005; July 2020-February 2021) and a temporal validation cohort (n = 501; February-March 2021). The internal cohort was randomly divided into a training set (n = 1,391) and a test set (n = 614). Candidate predictors were restricted to information routinely available at nurse triage. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression identified parsimonious predictors, which were entered into a multivariable logistic regression (LR) model. Six machine-learning (ML) algorithms were trained as benchmarks. Discrimination (AUC, AUPRC), calibration (calibration curves, Brier score), clinical utility (decision-curve analysis, standardised net benefit), and DeLong tests for AUC differences were evaluated. An integer risk score was derived from LR coefficients. Feature contributions were examined with SHAP values based on the LR model.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: LTC prevalence was 44.8% (899/2,005) in the internal cohort and ED mortality was 1.7% (34/2,005). LASSO retained 13 predictors: age, sex, mode of arrival, symptom onset time, cardiogenic chest pain (CCP), chest tightness, hypertension, diabetes, coronary artery disease (CAD), chronic kidney disease (CKD), cerebrovascular disease (CVD), shock index (SI), and Modified Early Warning Score (MEWS). The LR model showed stable discrimination-AUC 0.864 (95% CI 0.844-0.883) in training, 0.876 (0.849-0.904) in the test set, and 0.860 (0.825-0.896) in temporal validation-without statistically significant AUC superiority of more complex ML models on the test or validation sets (DeLong P > 0.05). In the test set, LR achieved the highest AUPRC (0.858), F1 score (0.792), and standardised net benefit (0.690), with the lowest Brier score (0.142). The integer score ranged from -3 to 49. At the Youden-optimal cut-off of 18.8, four CETS-aligned tiers were defined: Level IV (score < 6.4), Level III (6.4-18.8), Level II (18.8-32.1), and Level I (score > 32.1). SHAP analysis of the LR model ranked transportation, CCP, MEWS, SI, sex, and age among the strongest contributors.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: An internally and temporally validated, laboratory-free LR-based integer score showed discrimination and calibration comparable to more complex ML models, with clearer interpretability for ED nursing practice. The score is intended to support-not replace-clinical judgement. Multicentre external validation and prospective implementation studies are required before routine clinical adoption.

articles.title: Evaluation of Neonates Presenting to the Pediatric Emergency Department with Non-Birth-Related Trauma.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This study aimed to evaluate the mechanisms of non-birth-related trauma in term neonates (<28 days old) presenting to a tertiary pediatric emergency department and to propose preventive strategies.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The authors retrospectively reviewed term neonates diagnosed with trauma unrelated to birth who presented to the Pediatric Emergency Department of Gazi University Faculty of Medicine between June 2018 and December 2023.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: There were 78 neonates (55.1% male; mean age 18.0 ± 9.8 days) included in this study. All patients were brought by their parents in an outpatient setting. Falls were the leading cause of presentation (69.3%), most commonly involving strollers. Physical examination was unremarkable in 59% of cases. Cranial computed tomography was performed in 69.3%, revealing abnormalities in 40.7% of scans, whereas 12.8% did not undergo any imaging. A significant association was observed between PECARN risk stratification and both computed tomography (CT) utilization and detection of pathological findings. Most neonates (84.6%) were discharged home and the overall hospitalization rate was 7.7%.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Non-birth-related trauma in neonates is predominantly mild and associated with favorable outcomes. However, imaging utilization remains relatively high despite largely benign clinical presentations. The frequent use of CT, even in the presence of normal physical examination findings, reflects the clinical uncertainty inherent in neonatal neurological assessment and the limited applicability of existing pediatric decision rules in this age group. These findings underscore the need for more standardized neonatal trauma assessment pathways to support judicious imaging decisions, reduce unnecessary radiation exposure, and optimize patient safety.

articles.title: Prehospital whole blood transfusion in traumatic hemorrhagic shock: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Prehospital whole blood (WB) is increasingly used for traumatic hemorrhagic shock due to logistical and physiological advantages. This study synthesized evidence, including recent RCTs, to clarify its clinical efficacy.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Six major databases were searched through May 22, 2026. Eligible studies included RCTs and comparative cohorts of adult patients receiving prehospital WB versus standard care. Primary outcomes were 24-hour and 28/30-day mortality. Data were pooled using random-effects models to calculate risk ratios (RR) and mean differences (MD) with 95% CIs.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Synthesis of six studies (3 RCTs, 3 cohorts) involving 4040 patients (1558 WB; 2482 standard care) showed prehospital WB did not significantly decrease 24-hour mortality (RR 1.00; P = 0.98) or 28/30-day mortality (RR 1.09; P = 0.30). No differences were found in 6-hour or in-hospital mortality. However, WB significantly reduced red blood cell requirements within 24 h of hospital arrival (MD -0.97; P = 0.03), though this secondary signal lost statistical significance during sensitivity analysis. Safety outcomes (ARDS, stroke, thrombotic events) showed no significant differences, although estimates for rare events were imprecise. Certainty of evidence ranged from very low to moderate.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Prehospital WB was not associated with improved short- or long-term survival compared with standard care. A reduction in 24-hour red blood cell transfusion requirements after hospital arrival was observed; however, this secondary finding was highly sensitive to individual study weight and was driven primarily by observational cohorts at serious risk of bias.

articles.title: Fluoroscopy-assisted percutaneous management of posterior pelvic ring injuries via multiple transsacral and iliosacral screws in the supine position.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: When patients are positioned supine for percutaneous screw insertion to achieve posterior pelvic ring fixation, the edge of the operating table can impede screw insertion trajectories, thereby increasing the risk of cortical perforation, especially during iliosacral screw (ISS) placement. Multiple screw insertion might also potentially increase the risk of cortical perforation. The aim of this study was to evaluate the feasibility, safety, and efficacy of inserting multiple (≥2) transsacral screw (TSS) and ISS in the supine position via the application of specific surgical strategies and techniques developed in our institution.

abstract.label: PATIENTS AND METHODS
abstract.text: Patients who underwent stabilization of posterior pelvic ring injuries via percutaneous insertion of multiple TSS and/or ISS in the supine position between May 2018 and December 2025 were included in this study. Distinct screw insertion combination patterns at different vertebral levels, which were primarily determined by the variable anterior-posterior width of the transverse osseous pathway at the first sacrum, were employed for posterior pelvic ring fixation. Wound infection and neurovascular complications associated with screws insertion procedure were recorded. Postoperative CT scans were performed to assess the position of the screws. At follow-up, radiographic evaluations were performed to evaluate the complications including screw loosening, screw breakage, and non-union.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 149 large-diameter (≥7 mm) screws, including 123 TSSs and 26 ISSs, were inserted in a total of 69 consecutive patients. No wound infection and neurovascular complication associated with the screw insertion procedure were found postoperatively. Postoperative CT imaging demonstrated that all inserted screws were intraosseous. All patients were followed for an average of 19.5 months (range, 6.6-38 months). Only one screw (S2 TSS) breakage was noted, and no screw loosening and no bone nonunion occurred.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Fluoroscopy-assisted percutaneous multiple large-diameter screws (TSS and ISS) insertion for posterior pelvic ring injuries with the patient positioned supine has been confirmed to be a feasible, safe, and effective surgical procedure.

articles.title: Testicular torsion traction technique relieves acute testicular pain and may aid in manual detorsion: A case report.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.text: Testicular torsion is a urologic emergency caused by twisting of the spermatic cord, resulting in compromised testicular perfusion. Ischemia duration is the most important predictor of testicular salvage, and definitive surgical management should be rapidly pursued. While awaiting surgery, manual detorsion may restore blood flow and provide symptomatic relief. The testicular torsion traction technique (TTTT) is a bedside maneuver combining downward traction with external rotation of the affected testicle. A 14-year-old male presented to the emergency department with acute onset of 10/10 left testicular pain. Physical examination revealed variation in lie of the left testicle. The TTTT was performed, and symptoms immediately improved and then completely resolved. Doppler ultrasound revealed no evidence of torsion. Semi-elective bilateral orchidopexy performed one month later confirmed bilateral bell clapper deformity. This case further describes the TTTT for testicular detorsion and demonstrates its potential value as a temporizing measure, particularly in rural or low-resource settings with delayed access to ultrasound, surgery, or tertiary care.

articles.title: A Community Hospital Implementation of a Mobile Preoperative Peripheral Nerve Block Service in Non-OR Environments for Hip Fracture Patients.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Peripheral nerve blocks (PNB) are recognized as best practice for managing pain in older adults with fragility hip fractures. Despite strong evidence, the adoption of PNB pre-operation has been slow due to several implementation barriers. This study addresses this gap by describing the co-design and implementation of a preoperative Mobile PNB Service led by anesthesiology in a Canadian community hospital. We aim to: (1) provide a transferable, anesthesia focused implementation roadmap; (2) identify key implementation activities that enable the delivery of PNBs outside the operating room; and (3) report formative feasibility and evaluation outcomes (blocks delivered, pain levels, adverse events, and opioids administered before and after block delivery.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The mobile PNB service is comprehensively described to enable replicability following the Template for Intervention Description and Replication (TIDieR) checklist. Key design and implementation activities are identified by matching the activities with theory informed implementation functions from the Behavior Change Wheel (BCW). The formative outcomes were tracked alongside block delivery and abstracted from the patients' chart.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The multidisciplinary team led implementation activities primarily targeted enablement, education, and environmental restructuring to support the capability, opportunity, and motivation to deliver nerve blocks. The Mobile PNB Service was implemented feasibly, 76 blocks were delivered (44% Emergency Department (ED) and 56% ward) and safely, no procedure-related adverse events were observed. Early implementation was associated with increased uptake of preoperative PNBs and substantial reductions in patient-reported mean (SD) pain scores following block delivery from 7.1 (2.6) pre-block to 1.0 (2.0) post-block, and reduction in mean (SD) opioid administration following block delivery from 0.64 (0.90 milligrams per hour of oral morphine equivalents pre-block to 0.22 (0.49) milligrams per hour post-block.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: This study provides a replicable, theory-informed roadmap for closing the gap between guideline-recommended PNB and their delivery in non-operating room settings. An anesthesiology-led Mobile PNB Service was successfully implemented by addressing known system- and provider-level barriers using implementation frameworks. These findings underscore the value of theory-guided service design to identify essential components that enable behavior change and expand access to evidence-based analgesia for hip fracture patients.

articles.title: The Poisoned Patient, Part 1: Interpreting Vital Signs Through a Toxicologic Lens.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

articles.title: Influence of culturally and linguistically diverse status on emergency triage documentation among patients with confirmed sepsis: A qualitative content analysis.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Sepsis is a medical emergency, characterised by a dysregulated immune system response to infection. It requires a prompt and accurate clinical history to recognise and treat early. This process may be more complex when patients are from Culturally and Linguistically Diverse (CaLD) backgrounds. Linguistic and cultural barriers may impede the ability of a triage nurses in Emergency Departments (ED) to obtain adequate clinical information delaying the recognition of sepsis and initiation of the Sepsis Pathway. Therefore, this study explores how a CaLD background may influence sepsis recognition at triage through qualitative analysis of triage notes of patients with a confirmed diagnoses of sepsis in ED.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Data were collected from 1000 participants with confirmed sepsis in Greater Western Sydney, NSW Australia between January 2022 and May 2024. Data were analysed using a hybrid approach to qualitative content analysis, drawing on both inductive and deductive reasoning.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Three key themes were constructed: 1. Language and cultural barriers to clinical communication; 2. Arrival context shapes the depth of triage narratives; 3. Altered physiological and cognitive function influence symptom expression and compound language barriers.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: These three themes highlighted potential factors to timely recognition of sepsis in CaLD populations. Understanding and recognising these factors may further support timely assessment, accurate triage and early recognition of sepsis in CaLD populations.

articles.title: Meleney's gangrene triggered by suprapubic catheter dislodgment and urine extravasation: A case report and review of management strategies.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Necrotizing soft tissue infection represents a spectrum of bacterial infections that result in rapidly progressive, life-threatening tissue necrosis. Early diagnosis remains a challenge due to the rarity of the condition and variable presentation. Herein, we present a case of Meleney's gangrene managed at a tertiary healthcare facility in Nigeria.

abstract.label: CASE PRESENTATION
abstract.text: The patient presented to the emergency department with a 13-hour history of inability to pass urine associated with pain. Physical examination revealed a tender urinary bladder consistent with a diagnosis of acute urinary retention. Following multiple failed attempts at urethral catheterisation, an ultrasound-guided percutaneous suprapubic cystostomy (SPC) was performed. Four days after being discharged home, he came back with a complaint of a dislodged suprapubic tube and leakage of urine through the SPC stoma. Physical examination revealed mild peristomal skin discolouration and tenderness. He underwent an open suprapubic cystostomy. However, the skin discoloration progressed to Meleney's gangrene. Surgical debridement was performed, and broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy was initiated. The wound was later skin grafted after satisfactory wound care. However, most of the graft was lost, and the patient had successful secondary wound healing.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: We strongly believe that the dislodgement of the suprapubic tube and subsequent extravasation of urine into the tissue planes and the retropubic space were the likely precipitating events in our patient, especially given that the urine was infected. Chemicals in urine, such as urea and ammonia, can irritate tissue, leading to chemical cellulitis and inflammation. Additionally, the extravasated urine creates an ideal environment for microbial proliferation. Consequently, the combined chemical and bacterial assault potentiates the local inflammatory response, allowing infection to spread quickly along fascial planes. Successful treatment relies on surgical debridement, broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy, wound management, and supportive care.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This case report underscores the importance of proper suprapubic catheter placement to avoid dislodgement and urinary leak into subcutaneous tissue planes, which can trigger Meleney's gangrene. It provides a clear lesson that any suprapubic tube dislodgement must be regarded as high risk, warranting vigilant monitoring for signs of deep soft tissue infection.

articles.title: CCBE1 promotes wound healing in diabetic rats by improving the functional impairment of AD-MSCs induced by AGEs.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: The etiology of chronic and non-healing diabetic wounds is manifold; the progression of the non-healing phenotype is strongly associated with poor vascular networks. Mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) are reckoned as a promising therapy for wound healing, especially in angiogenesis. Here, we explored the role of CCBE1 in diabetic wound healing using human adipose-derived MSCs (hAD-MSCs).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Human adipose-derived hAD-MSCs were isolated and expanded through serial in vitro passaging. Cell proliferation and migration were evaluated using Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK8) and scratch wound assays, respectively. collagen, and calcium-binding EGF domain-containing protein 1 (CCBE1) and vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) expression were analyzed via western blotting. Functional studies of CCBE1 were conducted using siRNA-mediated knockdown and plasmid-driven overexpression approaches. Type 2 diabetes mellitus was induced in Sprague-Dawley rats through a high-fat/high-glucose diet combined with streptozotocin administration. Full-thickness excisional wounds were generated on the dorsal skin, and the effects of CCBE1 modulation in hAD-MSCs on wound closure were examined. Reepithelialization and angiogenesis were analyzed using histological and immunohistochemical methods. Protein levels of CCBE1 and vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) were quantified by western blotting.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: hAD-MSCs showed a gradual decrease in cell proliferation, migrationand increased apoptosis, during advanced glycation end products (AGEs) conditions; meanwhile, CCBE1 and VEGF expression decreased The downregulation of CCBE1 inhibited cell proliferation and migration, and enhanced apoptosis, while CCBE1 overexpression enhanced proliferation and migration, and reduced apoptosis. Compared with untransduced hAD-MSCs, local subcutaneous injection of CCBE1-overexpressing hAD-MSCs accelerated wound closure, enhanced angiogenesis and reepithelialization at the wound bed, and increased VEGF levels in wound tissues.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: CCBE1 overexpression promoted hAD-MSC proliferation and migration and reduced cell apoptosis in vitro and accelerated diabetic wound closure, reepithelialization, and angiogenesis by improving hAD-MSCs in vivo. These beneficial effects of CCBE1 overexpression in diabetic wound healing by hAD-MSCs were at least partially mediated by increased VEGF levels in wound tissues.

articles.title: Spontaneous resolution of cerebrospinal fluid obstruction due to intraventricular hemorrhage: A case report.

abstract.text: Obstructive hydrocephalus is a serious and potentially life-threatening condition caused by the temporary blockage of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) flow. Most cases require urgent intervention as spontaneous resolution is very uncommon. We present the case and brain imaging of a 63-year-old man who presented to the emergency department with complaint of headache, nausea, confusion, and dysarthria. Initial imaging showed a left caudate bleed with intraventricular hemorrhage and mild hydrocephalus secondary to obstruction of CSF in the aqueduct of Sylvius. External ventricular drain (EVD) was deferred due to mild symptoms and small intraventricular clot burden. The following day, he had marked improvement in mental status, and repeat head computed tomography showed spontaneous resolution of the obstruction without an EVD or intraventricular thrombolysis. This case demonstrates the importance of correlating clinical symptoms with imaging findings and close neuromonitoring. Mild symptoms, along with mild hydrocephalus and small clot burden, in addition to timely repeat imaging may avoid unnecessary invasive procedures.

articles.title: The influence of temperature on suicidality in youth: The role of insomnia.
articles.journal_full: The journal of climate change and health

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Suicide is the second leading cause of death among youth, with growing evidence linking higher ambient temperatures to increased suicidality - a concerning trend as global temperatures rise. Sleep disruption is a theorized mechanism, though clinical evidence is lacking.

abstract.label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
abstract.text: We performed a cross-sectional analysis of 5,590 pediatric patients (3-18 years) presenting to a psychiatric emergency department with and without suicidality (December 2018-March 2023). Seven-day averages of mean and minimum daily ambient temperatures and precipitation were obtained at home addresses from the PRISM Climate Group dataset. Logistic regression assessed insomnia as a moderator and mediator of the temperature-suicidality relationship, controlling for sociodemographic, diagnostic, and environmental variables. Negative controls included modeling suicidality using hypersomnia-temperature and insomnia-precipitation interactions.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Mean and minimum daily temperatures moderated the temperature-suicidality relationship only in those with insomnia (Mean Temperature: RR: 1.06 per 5°C [95% CI 1.01-1.06], p = 0.015; Minimum Temperature: RR: 1.06 per 5°C [95% CI 1.01-1.06], p = 0.010). Minimum temperature, a proxy for nighttime temperature, was associated with suicidality through insomnia in a mediation model (Indirect Pathway: OR: 1.05 [95% CI 1.00-1.11], p = 0.045), though mean temperature was not. No significant moderation occurred modeling suicidality with hypersomnia-temperature or insomnia-precipitation interactions.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This is the first clinical evidence that insomnia influences the heat-suicidality relationship in youth. Limitations include cross-sectional data that cannot establish temporal directionality of associations, heterogeneous suicidality outcomes, self-reported sleep data, and pandemic-era data collection. Larger mechanistic analyses of temperature, sleep, and suicidality are needed to understand climatic mental health impacts and develop interventions.

articles.title: Locked plate fixation versus non-operative management for three and four-part proximal humeral fractures in elderly; A randomized controlled trial.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: In elderly patients, the proximal humerus fracture is the third most prevalent fracture, following fractures of the hip and distal radius, and is significantly associated with osteoporosis. This research aimed to determine the functional and radiological outcomes of internal fixation of 3- and 4-part proximal humeral fractures by locked plates compared with the outcomes obtained by non-operative management in the elderly.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this prospective randomized trial, 52 elderly patients (≥65 years) with 3- or 4-part proximal humerus fractures were allocated to either nonoperative treatment with arm sling immobilization or operative fixation using a proximal humerus locking plate in Qena General Hospital from December 2020 to December 2023. Clinical and radiological assessments were conducted up to 12 months post-treatment, with functional outcomes measured by DASH and Constant scores.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Six months after surgery, the Conservative group had a significantly higher DASH score than the Operative group. At 12 months, the Conservative group had a lower DASH score and a higher total Constant score (p < 0.05). There was no significant variance in the incidence of SAI, stiffness, deformity, or AVN among the conservative and operative groups (p > 0.05). The complication rate was 13.4%, with 5.7% of cases related to conservative treatment and 7.7% to operative treatment.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Orthopaedic management of proximal humerus fractures requires proper evaluation, radiological views, patient age, and activity levels. Conservative treatment can provide good functional outcomes with a minimal complication rate, especially in elderly individuals.

articles.title: [Application effect of LLMs as decision-support tools in emergency burn treatment].
articles.journal: Zhonghua Shao Shang Yu Chuang Mian Xiu Fu Za Zhi
articles.journal_full: Zhonghua shao shang yu chuang mian xiu fu za zhi

abstract.text: Objective: To explore the application effect of large language models (LLMs) as decision-support tools in emergency burn treatment. Methods: This study was a cross-sectional study. A total of 100 burn patients meeting the inclusion criteria were admitted to the Department of Emergency Medicine of the Second Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang University School of Medicine between September 2025 and April 2026, including 52 males and 48 females, aged 34.5 (25.0, 56.8) years. Based on patients' discharge summaries, the diagnoses and treatment plans reviewed and confirmed by an expert panel, consisting of two emergency medicine physicians with associate senior titles and one burn and wound-repair specialist with a senior title from the hospital, were taken as the gold standard. Based on the gold standard and in a blind manner, two burn and wound-repair physicians with more than 5 years of working experience in the hospital used the Likert scale to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy and rationality of treatment plans, which were generated during May 25-28, 2026 for the aforementioned 100 patients by 4 LLMs (ChatGPT-5.5, Doubao-2.0-Pro, Qwen-3.6-Max-Preview, and Gemini 3.5 Flash) as well as 10 emergency medicine department junior physicians (EDJPs). The percentage of diagnostic accuracy scores and treatment plan rationality scores for the 100 patients were compared among EDJPs and the four LLMs; the percentage of diagnostic accuracy scores across patients with varying burn severities were also compared among EDJPs and the four LLMs; the consistency of diagnostic accuracy scores and treatment plan rationality scores were compared between the two evaluators. Results: The percentages of diagnostic accuracy scores for the 100 patients by Doubao-2.0-Pro, Gemini 3.5 Flash, ChatGPT-5.5, and Qwen-3.6-Max-Preview were 100% (100%, 100%), 100% (100%, 100%), 100% (50%, 100%), and 100% (50%, 100%), respectively, which were all significantly higher than the 100% (50%, 100%) by EDJPs (P<0.05). The treatment plan rationality scores for the 100 patients by Doubao-2.0-Pro, ChatGPT-5.5, and Gemini 3.5 Flash were 4.0 (4.0, 4.0), 4.0 (4.0, 4.0), and 4.0 (4.0, 4.0), respectively, which were all significantly higher than the 4.0 (3.0, 4.0) by EDJPs (P<0.05). The treatment plan rationality scores for the 100 patients by Doubao-2.0-Pro and ChatGPT-5.5 were significantly higher than the 4.0 (3.0, 4.0) by Qwen-3.6-Max-Preview (P<0.05). The percentages of diagnostic accuracy scores for patients with mild burns by Doubao-2.0-Pro, Gemini 3.5 Flash, and ChatGPT-5.5 were significantly higher than that by EDJPs (P<0.05); the percentages of diagnostic accuracy scores for patients with moderate burns by Doubao-2.0-Pro, Qwen-3.6-Max-Preview, and Gemini 3.5 Flash were significantly higher than that by EDJPs (P<0.05); the differences in percentages of diagnostic accuracy scores were not statistically significant among EDJPs and the four LLMs for patients with severe and extremely severe burns (P>0.05). Good consistency was observed for diagnostic accuracy scores between the two evaluators (with an interclass correlation coefficient of 0.821, with a 95% CI of 0.746-0.876), and moderate consistency was noted for treatment plan rationality scores (with an interclass correlation coefficient of 0.650, with a 95% CI of 0.522-0.749). Conclusions: Doubao-2.0-Pro, ChatGPT-5.5, and Gemini 3.5 Flash matched or even surpassed EDJPs in terms of diagnostic accuracy and treatment plan rationality for emergency burn patients, showing preliminary potential to serve as tools for second clinical opinions in burn care.

articles.title: [Artificial intelligence-enabled full-course diagnosis and treatment for patients with severe burns and wounds requiring repair: from risk prediction to causal inference].
articles.journal: Zhonghua Shao Shang Yu Chuang Mian Xiu Fu Za Zhi
articles.journal_full: Zhonghua shao shang yu chuang mian xiu fu za zhi

abstract.text: The diagnosis and treatment of severe burns and complex wounds require the coordinated management of local tissue injury, systemic pathophysiological changes, and sequential clinical interventions. Existing diagnostic and treatment pathways can support bedside evidence-based decision-making and allow clinicians to adjust treatment as a patient's condition evolves. However, limitations remain in the consistency of prehospital and primary-care assessments, the longitudinal integration of multimodal information, and the use of risk prediction results to support clinical decisions. Based on the clinical requirements of severe burn and complex wound care and the available evidences form artificial intelligence studies, this expert commentary examines the capability boundaries of current care pathways, the potential clinical benefits for different users, and the conditions required to extend risk prediction to constrained causal inference. We propose a full-course dynamic diagnostic and treatment framework comprising wound assessment, systemic monitoring, and clinical intervention. Standardized image analysis is used to assess wound area, depth, necrosis, infection, and healing trajectories. Time-series models integrate vital signs, laboratory measurements, inflammatory and infectious markers, metabolic and coagulation status, and organ function to continuously monitor the patient's systemic condition. At the same time, clinical interventions, including fluid resuscitation, anti-infective treatment, debridement and wound coverage, nutritional support, and rehabilitation, are aligned along a unified timeline to preserve the temporal relationships among changes in patient status, intervention timing, and clinical outcomes. Risk prediction is used to estimate potential clinical outcomes that may occur under the existing diagnostic and treatment pathways, whereas counterfactual simulation must be based on explicit causal assumptions, applicability conditions, uncertainty estimates, and boundaries of responsibility, and its results cannot be used directly as treatment prescriptions. The clinical value of artificial intelligence should be established through prospective studies that directly compare the effects of clinicians' independent judgments with those of their artificial intelligence-assisted judgments. In addition to discrimination, evaluation should include assessment time, inter-clinician agreement, calibration, warning lead time, alert and workflow burden, changes in clinical decisions, patient safety, and clinical outcomes. Addressing the capability boundaries of current care pathways, intelligent wound assessment, systemic risk monitoring, causal inference, and translational implementation and governance, this article discusses the pathways and boundaries of artificial intelligence integration into full-course diagnosis and treatment for patients with severe burns and wounds requiring repair.

articles.title: Impact of Preoperative Image Sharing and Anatomical Suitability on EVAR Outcomes for Ruptured Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: The influence of anatomical suitability on outcomes after endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) for ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm (rAAA) remains uncertain. This study evaluated the association between adherence to device instructions for use (IFU) and clinical outcomes after EVAR for rAAA.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We retrospectively reviewed 31 consecutive patients who underwent emergency EVAR for rAAA between August 2016 and June 2023. Anatomical suitability was assessed by retrospective computed tomography, and patients were classified as inside or outside IFU. The influence of preoperative image sharing (JOIN; Allm, Tokyo, Japan) on perioperative workflow was also evaluated, with patients divided into image-sharing and non-image-sharing groups. The primary outcome was reintervention; secondary outcomes included 30-day and overall mortality.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Twenty patients (64.5%) were inside IFU and eleven (35.5%) were outside IFU. Outside-IFU cases had shorter proximal neck length and greater neck angulation. Reintervention was more frequent outside IFU than inside IFU (63.6% vs. 10.0%, p <0.01), whereas 30-day mortality (18.2% vs. 10.0%, p = 0.601) and overall mortality (36.4% vs. 60.0%, p = 0.300) were not significantly different. Prehospital image sharing using the JOIN application was associated with shorter door-to-operating room time despite longer transfer distance.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: EVAR for rAAA may achieve acceptable early survival in selected outside-IFU cases; however, outside-IFU anatomy is associated with increased reintervention. Careful patient-specific selection and structured follow-up are essential.

articles.title: Point-of-care ultrasound identification of a Calvarial hemangioma in the emergency department: a case report.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.text: Calvarial intraosseous hemangiomas are rare, benign vascular tumors arising from the intrinsic vasculature of bone. They account for approximately 0.2% of all benign osseous neoplasms and 2% of calvarial tumors. They most commonly present as localized, progressive scalp swelling with headache and are diagnosed using computed tomography (CT) or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Reports describing the sonographic appearance of calvarial intraosseous hemangiomas are exceedingly limited, and no cases have been reported in which point-of-care ultrasound (PoCUS) was used for evaluation in the emergency department (ED) setting. We present the case of an otherwise healthy 22-year-old woman who presented to the ED with a four-day history of a tender right parietal scalp mass and localized headache. PoCUS demonstrated a well-circumscribed lesion arising from the calvarium with superficial swelling, rather than an isolated soft-tissue lesion which was suspected based on history and examination. An MRI was subsequently ordered and demonstrated an enhancing calvarial lesion favored to represent a calvarial intraosseous hemangioma. The patient was referred to neurosurgery for further evaluation and management. Although CT and MRI remain the diagnostic standards for calvarial intraosseous hemangiomas, this case demonstrates the potential value of PoCUS as a rapid bedside tool for distinguishing superficial scalp lesions from underlying osseous pathology and guiding prompt advanced imaging.

articles.title: Interpretable admission-stage machine learning for early Sepsis-3 identification in the emergency department.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Artificial intelligence-based clinical decision support systems have emerged as promising tools for improving early sepsis recognition in emergency departments. This study aimed to develop and evaluate interpretable machine learning models for identifying Sepsis-3-defined sepsis using routinely available admission-stage variables and to compare their performance with conventional biomarkers and the Systemic Inflammatory Response Syndrome (SIRS).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This secondary analysis used a publicly available prospective cohort of 1,572 adult emergency department patients with suspected community-onset sepsis. The outcome was Sepsis-3-defined sepsis. Thirteen demographic, physiological, and laboratory admission variables were evaluated. Following a stratified 70:30 train-test split, missing data were handled using multivariate imputation by chained equations, and feature selection was performed using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator logistic regression. Penalized logistic regression (LR), Explainable Boosting Machine (EBM), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) models were developed using five-fold cross-validation. Performance was evaluated by discrimination, classification, calibration, decision curve analysis, and explainability.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 1,572 adult patients, 560 met the Sepsis-3 criteria. In the internal holdout test set, AUROC values were 0.753 (LR), 0.763 (XGBoost), 0.767 (LightGBM), and 0.766 (EBM). Conventional biomarkers and SIRS showed lower discrimination (AUROC 0.599-0.693), whereas a biomarker-only logistic regression model achieved an AUROC of 0.710. No significant AUROC differences were observed among the machine learning models. LightGBM achieved the numerically highest AUROC and accuracy, whereas EBM achieved the highest sensitivity (0.845). Age, procalcitonin, oxygen saturation, respiratory rate, and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio were the most influential predictors.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Interpretable machine learning models based on routinely available emergency department admission variables provided moderate discrimination, clinically relevant sensitivity, and transparent predictor effects for identifying Sepsis-3-defined sepsis. Compared with conventional biomarkers, SIRS, and a biomarker-only logistic regression model, the machine learning models generally showed higher discrimination, although the magnitude and statistical significance of these differences varied across comparators. External validation is required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Associations between the standard deviation of apparent temperature and sudden cardiac arrest during the Taipei Marathon, 2013-2024.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Climate change has led to a discernible increase in the intensity of extreme weather events, contributing to growing public health concerns regarding temperature-related mortality and morbidity. Recently, there has been an increase in the number of sudden cardiac arrests (SCAs) occurring during annual Taipei Marathon events compared with previous years. This study aimed to explore the correlation between weather conditions and SCA risk in runners.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective observational study used data from the Taipei Marathon event held between 2013 and 2024 in Taiwan. We examined the relationship between the SCAs and weather conditions for each year using a Poisson regression model.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among the 95,866 full- and 220,580 half-marathoners, all SCAs occurred in Taiwanese runners. There were three SCAs in male marathoners (median age, 50 years). In half-marathon runners, 10 SCAs occurred (median age, 30 years), including nine males and one female. Each 1 °C increase in the standard deviation of apparent temperature (AT) over the 7-day time window (lag 0-6) was associated with an SCA incidence rate that was 6.63 times as high on race day (IRR = 6.63, 95% profile likelihood CI 1.85-52.11; LRT p < 0.001). The incidence rate was significantly higher during half-marathons than during full marathons (4.53 versus 3.13 per 100,000 participants) and among men than among women (5.17 versus 1.18 per 100,000). The highest proportion of SCA (61.5%) occurred in the final quarter of the race. Bystander-administered cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) was provided in all SCA events (100%). Automated external defibrillator shocks were delivered to 11 of 13 runners (84.6%). All 13 runners (100%) achieved return of spontaneous circulation in the field.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Greater short-term AT variability was associated with a higher incidence of SCA during Taipei Marathon events, suggesting that temperature variability over several days preceding and including race day may be associated with SCA occurrence. Runners should remain highly vigilant and take proactive measures under cold/high-risk weather conditions. The on-site presence of trained first responders to initiate CPR is mandatory at these events. A well-planned model of in-event emergency medical services is of vital importance in scenarios such as marathon events.

articles.title: Spinal Subdural Abscess in the Emergency Department: A Rare Diagnosis in an Immunocompetent Host.
articles.journal: J Am Coll Emerg Physicians Open
articles.journal_full: Journal of the American College of Emergency Physicians open

abstract.text: Spinal subdural abscess is an exceptionally rare and potentially life-threatening spinal infection characterized by the accumulation of purulent material between the dura and arachnoid mater. In contrast to the more common spinal epidural abscess, spinal subdural abscesses have been reported in fewer than 80 cases, often in pediatric, postoperative, or immunocompromised patients. This case represents the fourth documented instance of a spinal subdural abscess in an immunocompetent adult without identifiable risk factors or a known source of infection and the first reported in emergency medicine literature. A 60-year-old immunocompetent woman presented to the emergency department with atraumatic low back pain initially attributed to lumbar radiculopathy. She returned six days later with worsening bilateral radicular pain, urinary incontinence, and systemic symptoms. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed a large subdural fluid collection from T2 to L5, concerning for spinal subdural abscess. Emergent surgical decompression revealed frank purulence within the subdural space. Cultures grew Streptococcus intermedius, a rare pathogen in spinal infections. The patient completed an 8-week course of intravenous cefazolin and recovered fully with resolution of neurologic deficits. Spinal subdural abscesses can progress rapidly, causing widespread neurologic impairment due to the continuity of the subdural space. This case underscores the importance of maintaining a high index of suspicion for spinal infections in patients presenting with back pain and neurological deficits, even in immunocompetent patients. Early MRI and surgical consultation are essential to prevent irreversible neurological damage and optimize patient outcomes.

articles.title: Peer Support Workers to Improve Emergency Department Care Completion Among Patients Who Use Substances: A Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.journal: J Am Coll Emerg Physicians Open
articles.journal_full: Journal of the American College of Emergency Physicians open

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Assess feasibility of a randomized trial and the hypothesis that emergency department (ED) Peer support workers (Peers), who share personal lived experiences and resources, may decrease ED patients with substance use who leave before treatment completion (LBTC). Specific objectives included assessing operational feasibility, estimating recruitment rates, and seeking preliminary evidence of benefit to support the definitive trial.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Pragmatic, open-label pilot randomized trial over the initial 15 weeks of an ED Peer program. Shifts randomized 2:1 to Peer support or usual care.We analyzed patients aged 18-75 years with the 3 most common substance use-related presenting complaints: (1) localized swelling/redness, (2) withdrawal, and (3) substance misuse/intoxication.Feasibility outcomes were patient acceptance and recruitment rate. The primary measure was LBTC (shift level and patient level). Exploratory analyses evaluated naloxone kits and 48-hour ED revisits.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: There were 72 intervention shifts (391 visits) and 37 control shifts (198 visits). Patients had a median age of 44 (IQR 35-54); 71.3% were male.

abstract.label: FEASIBILITY
abstract.text: A total of 94.9% of patients accepted Peer support. The mean recruitment rate was 30 patient visits per week.

abstract.label: LBTC
abstract.text: Mean LBTC was 17.0% (SD 18.3%) among Peer shifts, and 23.1% (SD 22.8%) among control shifts, a difference of -6.1% (95% CI -14.6%, 2.4%).The Peer modestly impacted patient-level LBTC (OR 0.78 [95% CI 0.46, 1.32]). Among patients with substance misuse/intoxication or withdrawal, the Peer decreased odds of LBTC (21.4% vs 26.9%; OR 0.39 [95% CI 0.18, 0.84]).

abstract.label: EXPLORATORY
abstract.text: Peer interaction increased odds of receiving a naloxone kit (OR 2.33 [95% CI 1.34, 4.04]) and decreased 48-hour ED return visits (OR 0.46 [95% CI 0.22, 0.95]).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: An ED Peer may decrease LBTC among patients who use substances. A randomized trial is feasible.

articles.title: A Brush With Danger.
articles.journal: J Am Coll Emerg Physicians Open
articles.journal_full: Journal of the American College of Emergency Physicians open

articles.title: Physical examination of the cervical spine should be conducted in female athletes with a history of concussion.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Female athletes may be at increased risk of injury following sports-related concussion (SRC), even after symptom resolution. Residual cervical spine impairments have been proposed as a potential contributor; however, these have not been well characterised in female athletes. This study aimed to examine whether a history of SRC was associated with clinical assessments of the cervical spine in female athletes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this cross-sectional observational study, 156 elite and pre-elite female athletes from water polo, soccer, diving, rugby-7s and cycling/BMX were recruited. History of SRC within the previous 12 months was self-reported. Assessments included questionnaires and physical examination of the cervical spine, comprising range of motion, manual examination, joint position error (JPE) and maximal isometric neck strength. Between-group differences were examined using univariable statistical analyses.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Athletes with a history of SRC demonstrated a higher prevalence of reduced cervical range of motion, positive findings on manual examination, increased JPE and a history of headaches or migraines compared with athletes without concussion history. No deficits in maximal isometric neck strength were observed in athletes with a history of SRC.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Cervical spine impairments were more commonly observed in female athletes with a history of SRC within the previous 12 months, including in athletes who did not report current neck pain. These findings suggest consideration of targeted cervical spine assessment beyond symptom-based screening in athletes with a concussion history. Whether identification and management of cervical spine impairments influence subsequent injury risk requires investigation in prospective and interventional studies.

articles.title: Age-related reduction in D-dimer cut-off specificity: Diagnostic relevance in geriatric patients.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: D-dimer testing is widely used to exclude pulmonary embolism (PE), but its specificity declines sharply with age. Evidence in very old adults is limited, as most validation studies include few patients aged ≥80 years. This study aimed to identify and validate a clinically appropriate D-dimer threshold for geriatric patients.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Two large cohorts of adults evaluated for suspected PE in a Geriatric Emergency Department were included. The derivation cohort included 1617 patients; the validation cohort included 2861 patients. D-dimer performance was assessed using ROC analysis, and specificity was compared across the conventional 500 μg/L FEU cut-off, the age-adjusted threshold, a fixed 1000 μg/L FEU threshold, and the optimized threshold. PE diagnosis was confirmed by CT pulmonary angiography.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: D-dimer levels increased with age, inflammation, and renal dysfunction. In the derivation cohort, the conventional cut-off showed low specificity, particularly in patients aged ≥90 years. The age-adjusted threshold improved performance but remained insufficient in the oldest age groups. An optimized threshold of 1050 μg/L FEU provided the best balance between sensitivity (100% in the derivation cohort and 97.8% in the validation cohort) and specificity, with a negative predictive value of 99.8%. This threshold correctly reclassified 23% of patients who were false-positive at the 500 μg/L FEU cut-off.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In very old adults, the conventional D-dimer cut-off is clinically inadequate, and the age-adjusted threshold remains suboptimal. A threshold of 1050 μg/L FEU, validated in two very old geriatric cohorts, offers a safer and more specific alternative for ruling out PE in geriatric emergency care.

articles.title: The impact of an app-delivered mindfulness-based intervention on resting-state functional connectivity in pediatric concussion: a pilot study.

abstract.label: RATIONALE
abstract.text: Concussion disrupts brain connectivity, and effective treatments remain limited. Mindfulness-based interventions (MBIs) may influence functional connectivity (FC) of networks affected by concussion, but pediatric trials are lacking. This study investigated whether an app-delivered MBI produced greater FC changes than a sham condition across the default mode (DMN), salience (SN), and central executive (CEN) networks.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This randomized clinical trial (NCT05105802) recruited participants aged 12.00-17.99 years from the emergency department or interdisciplinary concussion clinic, then randomly assigned them to MBI or cognitive sham. Brain imaging sessions occurred at 72 h and 4 weeks post-concussion. Region-of-interest and seed-to-voxel analyses examined Group × Time interactions in FC across DMN, SN, and CEN (p < 0.050 FDR ).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Thirty-six participants were included (MBI: n = 16, median [IQR] age = 14.23 [13.52-15.65] years, 31% female; Sham: n = 20, median [IQR] age = 14.05 [13.13-16.26] years, 45% female). Intention-to-treat analyses revealed significant Group × Time interactions across networks. DMN-CEN FC patterns differed, with MBI participants showing diminished FC. Within DMN, four clusters showed significant interactions (p < 0.050 FDR ), three exhibiting larger FC reductions at 4 weeks in MBI participants. MBI participants showed greater FC increase in one SN cluster (p = 0.040 FDR ) and larger FC decrease in one CEN cluster (p = 0.024 FDR ) at 4 weeks. Per-protocol analyses identified one significant DMN cluster (p < 0.001 FDR ) where MBI participants exhibited greater FC increases.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Mindfulness-based intervention training led to changes in FC in networks implicated in concussion recovery. Larger studies are needed to support these findings.

abstract.label: CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract.text: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05105802, identifier NCT05105802.

articles.title: Gastrointestinal mucormycosis with no classical immunosuppression and the potential for Qat leaves chewing as an unidentified risk factor: a case report.

abstract.text: Gastrointestinal mucormycosis is a rare, life-threatening invasive fungal infection that is often diagnosed late because of nonspecific clinical and endoscopic findings. Khat or Qat (Catha edulis) leaves may harbor environmental fungi, including Mucor species, and chronic chewing may contribute to gastrointestinal mucosal injury. However, a possible association between Qat use and gastrointestinal mucormycosis has not been established. We report a case of a 60-year-old man with diet-controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus and long-standing Qat chewing who was admitted after an out-of-hospital cardiac arrest secondary to acute myocardial infarction. He had no history of malignancy, transplantation, neutropenia, or immunosuppressive therapy. Return of spontaneous circulation was achieved after 34 min of cardiopulmonary resuscitation, followed by temporary venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation. On hospital day 14, coffee-ground material was observed through the nasogastric tube, accompanied by a decline in hemoglobin from 14.0 to 9.5 g/dL. Esophagogastroduodenoscopy revealed a fungating, ulcerated lesion involving the gastric fundus and body. Histopathological examination demonstrated extensive necrosis, angioinvasion, and broad, ribbon-like, pauci-septate fungal hyphae with irregular branching, consistent with gastric mucormycosis. Intravenous liposomal amphotericin B was initiated at 8 mg/kg/day. Gastrointestinal bleeding resolved without surgery. Repeat endoscopy one month later showed marked healing, and follow-up biopsy revealed no residual fungal elements. The patient completed six weeks of antifungal therapy and achieved clinical and histopathological resolution. Fungal culture and molecular identification were not performed, precluding species-level confirmation.‏ In conclusion, this case describes gastric mucormycosis in a patient without profound immunosuppression but with severe physiological stress and chronic Qat exposure. Critical illness, gastric hypoperfusion, and mucosal disruption may have facilitated fungal invasion. Qat chewing is presented as a hypothesis-generating factor because of possible fungal contamination of leaves and repeated mucosal injury; nevertheless, causality cannot be inferred from a single case. Further microbiological and epidemiological studies are required to investigate this potential association.

articles.title: The Multifaceted Burden of Dog Bite Injuries: A Retrospective Study From an Oral and Maxillofacial Surgical Unit.
articles.journal_full: Journal of oral and maxillofacial surgery : official journal of the American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Dog bite injuries (DBIs) are a common cause of facial trauma injuries requiring oral and maxillofacial surgery (OMS) input. They can present a dual burden of physical trauma and long-term psychological morbidity, yet these effects remain underrecognized and under-supported.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: This study aims to quantify the OMS workload associated with DBI's and identify the physical and psychological outcomes experienced by victims of these injuries.

abstract.label: STUDY DESIGN, SETTING, SAMPLE
abstract.text: Retrospective case series of dog-related injuries presenting to the OMS department from January 2020 to February 2025. The study was conducted in the OMS department of St Richard's Hospital, Chichester, UK. The exclusion criteria were nondog-related injuries, nonbite injuries from dogs, wounds not in the face or neck region, or other indications of admission.

abstract.label: PREDICTOR VARIABLE
abstract.text: Not applicable.

abstract.label: MAIN OUTCOME VARIABLE
abstract.text: The primary outcome was OMS service workload from head and neck DBIs measured by emergency department presentations, need for operative management, and operative time. The secondary outcome variable was long-term morbidity defined as the presence of persistent physical complications and psychological sequelae following the DBI.

abstract.label: COVARIATES
abstract.text: Subject demographics - age and sex. Injury characteristics - time of presentation, number, location, and type of wound. Dog-related and bite-related characteristics such as relationship of the dog to the victim, provocation, and breed of the dog.

abstract.label: ANALYSES
abstract.text: Descriptive statistics summarize sample characteristics.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: During the study interval, 3,097 subjects presented with animal-related injuries, of whom 784 (25.31%) sustained dog bites. Ninety-one (11.61%) subjects met the inclusion criteria, all requiring OMS assessment. Operative treatment was required in 73 (80.22%) subjects, of whom 40(44.0%) required a procedure under general anesthesia. The mean operative time was 30.8 ± 22.3 minutes. Of the 91 subjects included in the study, 55 (60.44%) completed the telephone survey. Among these 55 respondents, 22 (40%) reported physical complications and 25 (45.45%) reported psychological complications. Only 2 of the 55 respondents (3.64%) had received psychological support.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE
abstract.text: DBIs contribute to OMS workload, frequently require operative management, and may be associated with persistent physical and psychological morbidity. The findings suggest a potential role for greater emphasis on psychological support and strengthened prevention strategies.

articles.title: Evaluation of correlation between hip shoulder width ratio and sensory level of subarachnoid block in adult patients - A prospective observational study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND AND AIMS
abstract.text: Easily measurable anthropometric parameters may aid in predicting the level of spinal anaesthesia. Some studies have demonstrated a significant correlation between hip-shoulder width ratio (HSR) and level of spinal anaesthesia in lateral position. We hypothesised that even sitting position for subarachnoid injection will result in positive correlation between HSR and sensory level of spinal anaesthesia. So, we aimed to study correlation between HSR and sensory level of subarachnoid block in sitting position after administering 3 ml of 0.5% hyperbaric levobupivacaine.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: After institutional ethics committee approval and trial registration, 58 patients aged 18 to 60 years and of American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status I and II were included. The primary objective was to assess the relationship between HSR and the sensory block level. The secondary objectives included correlation between patient's age, height, weight, body mass index (BMI), vertebral column length, and sensory level. Descriptive analysis was performed using mean and standard deviation for quantitative variables. Pearson correlation coefficient was used to evaluate the association between quantitative variables.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Higher HSR correlated moderately with higher sensory block levels (r = 0.550, P < 0.001). Multiple linear regression analysis demonstrated that HSR, height, and BMI have statistically significant effects on the spread of spinal anaesthesia with HSR being the strongest factor.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: HSR is a simple, reliable predictor of sensory block height with hyperbaric levobupivacaine in adult patients.

articles.title: Direct-to-implant reconstruction as a cost-efficient option in patients aged 65 years and older.
articles.journal_full: Journal of plastic, reconstructive & aesthetic surgery : JPRAS

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Direct-to-implant (DTI) is a single-stage breast reconstruction technique. Data support its use in older patients, but most studies have focused on surgical outcomes rather than resource use. We compared costs, resource use, and outcomes between single-stage DTI and two-stage tissue expander (TE) reconstruction in patients aged ≥65 years.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A single-center retrospective review included patients ≥65 years who underwent implant-based breast reconstruction (2009-2023). Patients were matched 1:2 (DTI:TE) using Mahalanobis distance on age, body mass index, and history of smoking, radiation, chemotherapy, diabetes, and hypertension. Total cost was the sum of hospital costs spanning the index operation to one year after the final planned reconstruction, including costs for operative time, surgical materials, length of stay, emergency room visits, readmissions, and reoperations. Outcomes were analyzed using cluster-robust gamma regression with a log link and logistic regression adjusting for implant plane, laterality, and baseline characteristics.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The matched cohort included 30 DTI and 58 TE patients. DTI was associated with lower costs ($12,379 ± $5749 vs. $16,653 ± $6859; p=0.003) and shorter operative time (201 ± 100 vs. 353 ± 115 min; p<0.001). After adjustment, DTI continued to be associated with 15% lower costs (p=0.03), driven by a 36% shorter operating room time (p<0.001). The odds of any complication did not differ (p=0.22) CONCLUSION: DTI reconstruction was associated with lower costs and shorter operative time without increased risk of complications, supporting DTI as a reasonable lower-resource option for older patients.

articles.title: Fatal pedestrian injury secondary to rupture of a right coronary artery aneurysm: A case report.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Coronary artery aneurysm (CAA) rupture is a rare but life-threatening condition that typically presents as acute coronary syndrome or with hemodynamic collapse. Distinguishing whether severe trauma is the primary event or secondary to a preceding medical catastrophe poses a significant diagnostic challenge in the emergency setting.

abstract.label: CASE PRESENTATION
abstract.text: An 85-year-old woman, found crouched on a street, was struck by a truck and was transported to the emergency department. On arrival, she was unconscious but hemodynamically stable. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography revealed a ruptured right coronary artery aneurysm with active extravasation and surrounding hematoma, along with multiple severe traumatic injuries, including subarachnoid hemorrhage and hemopneumothorax. The patient died several hours after aggressive resuscitation.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This case illustrates an extremely rare scenario where aneurysmal rupture likely preceded the traumatic event, leading to secondary blunt trauma. This emphasizes the critical importance of considering primary vascular emergencies as underlying causes in trauma patients who present with atypical findings.

articles.title: Dynamic changes in quadriceps and diaphragm thickness for early diagnosis of ICU-acquired weakness in elderly ICU patients: a prospective bedside ultrasound study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To investigate the value of bedside ultrasound in dynamically monitoring quadriceps and diaphragm thickness for early diagnosis of ICU-acquired weakness (ICU-AW) in elderly critically ill patients.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This prospective observational study enrolled elderly patients (aged ≥60 years) with an expected ICU stay of ≥7 days. Bedside ultrasound was performed on days 1 (D1), 3, 5, and 7 after ICU admission to measure rectus femoris cross-sectional area (RF-CSA), rectus femoris muscle layer thickness (RF-MLT), vastus intermedius muscle layer thickness (VI-MLT), end-inspiratory diaphragm thickness (DTei), and end-expiratory diaphragm thickness (DTee). Muscle strength was assessed using the Medical Research Council (MRC) sum score. The rates of change of each parameter were compared between the ICU-AW group (MRC ≤ 48) and non-ICU-AW group. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were used to evaluate predictive performance.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 74 enrolled patients, 52 (70.3%) developed ICU-AW. No significant differences in baseline ultrasound parameters were found between groups. The rate of change of RF-MLT on D5 and D7 and the rate of change of DTee on D7 were significantly different between groups (P = 0.049, 0.021, and 0.009, respectively). The rate of change of DTee on D7 showed the strongest negative correlation with MRC score (r = -0.413, P < 0.001). ROC analysis showed that the D7 relative change in DTee had the numerically highest AUC (0.693, 95% CI: 0.556-0.830), with an optimal cutoff value of a decrease ≥6.07% (sensitivity 73.1%, specificity 59.1%), while RF-MLT yielded an AUC of 0.672 with a cutoff value of a decrease ≥3.45% (sensitivity 50.0%, specificity 86.4%). However, the difference between the two AUCs was small (0.021) and not formally tested, and the low specificity (59.1%) limits its clinical utility.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Progressive quadriceps and diaphragm atrophy occurs early in elderly ICU patients. The D7 relative change in DTee showed the numerically highest AUC among the evaluated parameters, suggesting modest discriminatory ability for ICU-AW and warranting further validation. Dynamic muscle ultrasound monitoring is feasible and reproducible at the bedside.

articles.title: Validation of the Pediatric Advanced Weight Prediction in the Emergency Room Extra Large Mid-Arm Circumference scale in Turkish children.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: This study aimed to validate the Pediatric Advanced Weight Prediction in the Emergency Room Extra Large-Mid-Arm Circumference (PAWPER XL-MAC) weight estimation scale in Turkish children by evaluating its accuracy, agreement, and validity across age groups. We assessed the scale's performance using mid-arm circumference (MAC), habitus status (HS), and height to predict weight, while examining age- and gender-related differences.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This study included pediatric patients (aged 0-18 years) who presented to a pediatric surgery outpatient clinic from December 2024 to April 2025. Data on demographics, height, weight, MAC, and clinician-assigned HS (1-7) were collected. PAWPER XL-MAC estimated weights were calculated. Accuracy was assessed using percentage within 10% (PW10) and percentage within 20% (PW20). Analyses included descriptive stats, Pearson correlations, t-tests/Welch's t-tests, ANOVA, multiple regression, Bland-Altman plots, and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) for validity measures. SPSS, R, and Jamovi were used.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The cohort comprised 323 boys (65.8%) and 168 girls (34.2%), for a total of 491 patients, with infants (0-2 years) forming the largest group (41.8%). Significant gender differences were observed in MAC and weight (p < 0.01). The multiple linear regression model (weight∼MAC + height + HS) demonstrated a strong fit (R2 = 0.878). Overall, PW10 was 10.8%, and PW20 was 21.0%, with marked age-dependent variation, with moderate performance in schoolers (PW10: 10.1%, PW20: 22.2%) and the highest in adolescents (PW10: 41.9%, PW20: 81.7%). MAC-HS agreement showed a moderate-to-weak positive association (gamma = 0.226). PCA revealed a single dominant factor explaining 62.4% of variance, with strong loadings for weight (0.89) and MAC (0.85). CFA proxy indices indicated acceptable-to-good model fit (comparative fit index ∼0.92-0.95, standardized root mean square residual ∼0.06-0.08).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The PAWPER XL-MAC scale shows acceptable structure validity in Turkish children but has age-related accuracy issues, especially in younger groups. Age-specific adjustments are recommended to improve reliability for emergency weight estimation and drug dosing in children.

articles.title: Clinical significance of controlling nutritional status score in predicting ICU admission, prolonged hospitalization, and in-hospital mortality in emergency sepsis: a single-center retrospective study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Sepsis is associated with high mortality in critically ill patients. Existing prognostic tools are often complex or require specialized testing. This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic value of the Controlling Nutritional Status (CONUT) score in patients with sepsis in the emergency department.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective analysis of 1,200 sepsis patients admitted to the emergency department of the Affiliated Changsha Central Hospital, Hengyang Medical School, University of South China from January 2020 to June 2025 was conducted. Kaplan-Meier analysis, multivariable Cox regression, restricted cubic splines (RCS), receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA) were employed to evaluate the associations between the CONUT score and ICU admission, prolonged hospitalization, and in-hospital all-cause mortality. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses were performed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Time-dependent Cox regression revealed that each one-point increase in the CONUT score was associated with an 11% increase in the risk of in-hospital mortality (HR = 1.11, 95% CI:1.02-1.21). After adjusting for potential confounders, logistic regression analysis further demonstrated that, the CONUT score was significantly associated with ICU admission (OR = 1.16, 95% CI: 1.09-1.23) and prolonged hospitalization (OR = 1.11, 95% CI: 1.05-1.17). RCS revealed linear positive correlations. ROC analysis showed that CONUT was superior to SOFA for predicting prolonged hospitalization, and combining CONUT with SOFA enhanced predictive performance. DCA indicated the combined model provided the highest clinical net benefit. Advanced age, diabetes, and mechanical ventilation modified the associations between CONUT and certain outcomes.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Elevated CONUT scores are independently associated with adverse outcomes in emergency department sepsis patients, serving as a simple prognostic indicator for early risk stratification.

articles.title: Reducing rural health inequity through drone-based delivery: a spatial multi-criteria decision framework prioritizing epidemiological vulnerability in hub location.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To alleviate spatial health inequities in rural areas by optimizing unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) medical hub location based on an epidemiological vulnerability-driven approach, correcting for the tendency of current logistics-centric models to overlook high-need rural populations.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A spatial multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) framework was developed for a simulated rural-urban fringe experiencing severe demographic aging. We defined a novel Epidemiological Vulnerability Index (EVI) incorporating three core dimensions: demographic aging, chronic disease burden (e.g., cardiovascular risks), and baseline healthcare deprivation (ground EMS delay). The framework integrates Geographic Information Systems (GIS) with the enhanced two-step floating catchment area (E2SFCA) method, Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP), and Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) to rank and allocate highly-prioritized UAV hub sites across 400 grid cells. All results are derived from a calibrated simulation environment and should be interpreted as model-based projections rather than empirical observations.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Simulation results indicated that the "Digital Inverse Care Law" emerged naturally under traditional logistics models, which allocated 85% of hubs to low-vulnerability urban centers. In contrast, the EVI-driven framework strategically anchored 65% of hubs in deep rural pockets. Under the baseline parameter assumptions, this reallocation of UAV hubs reduced the simulated average rural emergency response time by 74.8% (from 45.2 to 11.4 min) in the model. The 11.4-min figure represents UAV delivery time to the incident location, not complete emergency intervention time. This modeled improvement brought an estimated 88.4% of the highly vulnerable aging population into the "Golden 15-Minute" survival window within the simulation.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: By embedding epidemiological metrics into spatial planning, this framework provides a decision-support tool that is traceable and reproducible for health policymakers, based on model outputs rather than empirical field validation. It illustrates how targeted digital health infrastructure deployment could, under the model assumptions, contribute to narrowing the rural-urban emergency health divide. These findings are contingent on the specific model assumptions and require field validation and formal health-economic evaluation before real-world implementation.

articles.title: Organ donation after euthanasia starting at home: a mixed-methods study of preliminary nationwide Dutch experiences.
articles.journal_full: Transplant international : official journal of the European Society for Organ Transplantation

abstract.text: Organ Donation after Euthanasia starting at Home (ODEH) initiates the euthanasia trajectory at home with deep sedation, followed by transfer to the hospital for completion of euthanasia and organ procurement. We evaluated all eight Dutch ODEH procedures up to February 2024 using a mixed-methods design: descriptive analysis of anonymized case data (Dutch Transplant Foundation and hospital records) and semi-structured interviews (November 2023-February 2024) with involved professionals. All procedures were performed in three hospitals. Patients had neurodegenerative disease (n = 6) or psychiatric disorders (n = 2) and were aged from the mid-30s to the early-70s (mean 50.4 years). Professionals highlighted strict separation of euthanasia and donation decisions, time-critical coordination between home and hospital, variation in sedation/anesthesia and transport modality (regular ambulance vs. mobile ICU), regional constraints in staffing and infrastructure, emotional impact on professionals, and registry/coding considerations (including HSMR). ODEH is feasible within the existing Dutch legal framework and is valued for enabling a home farewell without compromising donation. A flexible practice manual defining core safeguards and decision points may support consistent implementation.

articles.title: A novel nomogram for predicting subsyndromal delirium in critically ill patients with diabetes.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND AND AIMS
abstract.text: This study aimed to develop and validate a nomogram for predicting subsyndromal delirium (SSD) risk in critically ill patients with diabetes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Critically ill adult patients with diabetes were retrospectively included in the emergency department of Peking Union Medical College Hospital from January 2025 to December 2025. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses identified independent predictors for SSD. A nomogram was constructed based on these predictors. The model's performance was assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 297 patients with diabetes were included and the overall incidence of SSD was 38.7%. Univariate and multivariate analysis identified six independent predictors: higher NRS score, RASS score, APACHE II score, PSQI score, random blood glucose level at admission, and lower Barthel index. The nomogram incorporating these factors demonstrated good discrimination, with an AUC of 0.922 (95% CI: 0.891-0.953). Calibration curves showed good agreement between predicted and observed probabilities, and DCA indicated favorable clinical utility.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: We developed and internally validated a nomogram for predicting SSD in critically ill patients with diabetes. The model may be useful for risk stratification, but prospective and external validation are required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Quantification of blood-based neurovascular unit biomarkers: an analytical platform comparison study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Hypoxic ischemic brain injury (HIBI) remains a significant cause of morbidity and mortality in patients following cardiac arrest. Many international guidelines for HIBI prognostication advocate for a multimodal approach with inclusion of blood-based biomarkers. However, advancements in analytical technology have increased uncertainty in selecting the optimal quantification tool and impeded application of these results across platforms in accordance with amalgamated prognostication thresholds.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a post hoc analysis of a prospective observational cohort study in 32 critically ill patients undergoing withdrawal of life-sustaining therapies.
